title.en: Volume 66 Biographies 56: Du Sengming, Zhou Wenyu, Hou Zhen, Hou Andou, Ouyang Wei, Huang Fa, Chun Yuliang, Zhang Zhaoda, Wu Mingche
title.raw: 卷六十六 列傳第五十六 杜僧明 周文育 侯瑱 侯安都 歐陽頠 黃法𣰰 淳于量 章昭達 吳明徹 Volume 66 Biographies 56: Du Sengming, Zhou Wenyu, Hou Zhen, Hou Andou, Ouyang Wei, Huang Fa, Chun Yuliang, Zhang Zhaoda, Wu Mingche

sentences.zh: 列傳第五十六

translations.literal: Biographies 56
translations.idiomatic: the 56th year of Biography

sentences.zh: 杜僧明周文育侯瑱侯安都歐陽頠黃法奭淳于量章昭達吳明徹

translations.literal: Du Sengming, Zhou Wenyu, Hou Zhen, Hou Andou, Ouyang Wei, Huang Fa, Chun Yuliang, Zhang Zhaoda, Wu Mingche
translations.idiomatic: Du Sengming, Zhou Wenyu, Hou Zhen, Hou Andou, Ouyang Wei, Huang Fa, Chun Yuliang, Zhang Zhaoda, and Wu Mingche

sentences.zh: 形貌眇小而有膽氣，善騎射。

translations.literal: He was slight and small in appearance but had courage and spirit, and he was skilled at riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was slight and small in appearance but had courage and spirit, and he was skilled at riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 梁大同中，盧安興為廣州刺史、南江督護，僧明與兄天合及周文育並為安興所啟，請與俱行。

translations.literal: During the Datong era of Liang, Lu Anxing was inspector of Guangzhou and commander-protector of Nanjiang; Sengming, his elder brother Tianhe, and Zhou Wenyu were all recommended by Anxing, who requested that they go with him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Datong era of Liang, Lu Anxing was inspector of Guangzhou and commander-protector of Nanjiang; Sengming, his elder brother Tianhe, and Zhou Wenyu were all recommended by Anxing, who requested that they go with him.

sentences.zh: 頻征俚獠有功，為新州助防。

translations.literal: They repeatedly campaigned against the Li and Lao and had merit, and Sengming became assistant defender of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: They repeatedly campaigned against the Li and Lao and had merit, and Sengming became assistant defender of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 天合亦有材幹，預在征伐。

translations.literal: Tianhe also had ability and took part in campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Tianhe also had ability and took part in campaigns.

sentences.zh: 安興死，僧明復副其子子雄。

translations.literal: When Anxing died, Sengming again served as deputy to his son Zixiong.
translations.idiomatic: When Anxing died, Sengming again served as deputy to his son Zixiong.

sentences.zh: 及交州豪士李賁反，逐刺史蕭諮。

translations.literal: When Li Ben, a powerful man of Jiaozhou, rebelled and expelled Inspector Xiao Zi,
translations.idiomatic: When Li Ben, a powerful man of Jiaozhou, rebelled and expelled Inspector Xiao Zi,

sentences.zh: 諮奔廣州，臺遣子雄與高州刺史孫冏討賁。

translations.literal: Xiao Zi fled to Guangzhou, and the court sent Zixiong and Gaozhou Inspector Sun Jiong to campaign against Li Ben.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zi fled to Guangzhou, and the court sent Zixiong and Gaozhou Inspector Sun Jiong to campaign against Li Ben.

sentences.zh: 時春草已生，瘴癘方起，子雄請待秋討之，廣州刺史新渝侯蕭映不聽，蕭諮又促之，子雄等不得已，遂行。

translations.literal: At the time the spring grasses had already grown and miasmal illness was just arising; Zixiong asked to wait until autumn to attack him, but Guangzhou Inspector Xiao Ying, Marquis of Xinyu, would not listen, and Xiao Zi also pressed him, so Zixiong and the others had no choice and set out.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the spring grasses had already grown and miasmal illness was just arising; Zixiong asked to wait until autumn to attack him, but Guangzhou Inspector Xiao Ying, Marquis of Xinyu, would not listen, and Xiao Zi also pressed him, so Zixiong and the others had no choice and set out.

sentences.zh: 至合浦，死者十六七，眾並憚役潰散，禁之不可，乃引其餘兵退還。

translations.literal: When they reached Hepu, six or seven out of ten had died; the men all dreaded the campaign and scattered in collapse, and when they could not be restrained, he led the remaining troops back.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Hepu, six or seven out of ten had died; the men all dreaded the campaign and scattered in collapse, and when they could not be restrained, he led the remaining troops back.

sentences.zh: 蕭諮啟子雄及冏與賊交通，逗遛不進，梁武帝敕於廣州賜死。

translations.literal: Xiao Zi reported that Zixiong and Jiong had dealings with the rebels and lingered without advancing, and Emperor Wu of Liang ordered that they be granted death in Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zi reported that Zixiong and Jiong had dealings with the rebels and lingered without advancing, and Emperor Wu of Liang ordered that they be granted death in Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 子雄弟子略、子烈並豪俠，家屬在南江。

translations.literal: Zixiong’s younger brothers Zilüe and Zilie were both bold men of knightly spirit, and their households were in Nanjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiong’s younger brothers Zilüe and Zilie were both bold men of knightly spirit, and their households were in Nanjiang.

sentences.zh: 天合謀於眾曰：「盧公累葉待遇我等亦甚厚矣，今見枉死而不能為報，非丈夫也。

translations.literal: Tianhe planned with the group, saying, “Lord Lu has treated us very generously over successive generations; now, seeing him wrongfully killed and being unable to repay him is not the conduct of men.
translations.idiomatic: Tianhe planned with the group, saying, “Lord Lu has treated us very generously over successive generations; now, seeing him wrongfully killed and being unable to repay him is not the conduct of men.

sentences.zh: 我弟僧明萬人之敵，若圍州城，召百姓，誰敢不從。

translations.literal: My younger brother Sengming is a match for ten thousand men; if we surround the provincial city and summon the people, who would dare not follow?
translations.idiomatic: My younger brother Sengming is a match for ten thousand men; if we surround the provincial city and summon the people, who would dare not follow?

sentences.zh: 城破，斬二侯，然後待臺使至，束手詣廷尉，死猶勝生。

translations.literal: Once the city is broken, we will behead the two marquises, and afterward wait for the court envoy to arrive, bind our hands, and go to the Chamberlain for Law Enforcement; such a death would still be better than life.
translations.idiomatic: Once the city is broken, we will behead the two marquises, and afterward wait for the court envoy to arrive, bind our hands, and go to the Chamberlain for Law Enforcement; such a death would still be better than life.

sentences.zh: 縱其不捷，亦無恨矣。」

translations.literal: Even if it does not succeed, there will be no regret.”
translations.idiomatic: Even if it does not succeed, there will be no regret.”

sentences.zh: 眾咸忼慨曰：「是所願也，唯足下命之！」

translations.literal: The men all said indignantly, “This is what we desire; only give the command, sir!”
translations.idiomatic: The men all said indignantly, “This is what we desire; only give the command, sir!”

sentences.zh: 乃與周文育等率眾結盟，奉子雄弟子略為主，以攻刺史蕭映。

translations.literal: He then led the men with Zhou Wenyu and the others, formed a covenant, honored Zixiong’s younger brother Zilüe as their leader, and attacked Inspector Xiao Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He then led the men with Zhou Wenyu and the others, formed a covenant, honored Zixiong’s younger brother Zilüe as their leader, and attacked Inspector Xiao Ying.

sentences.zh: 子略頓城南，天合頓城北，僧明、文育分據東西，吏人並應之。

translations.literal: Zilüe encamped south of the city, Tianhe encamped north of the city, and Sengming and Wenyu separately occupied the east and west; officials and people all responded to them.
translations.idiomatic: Zilüe encamped south of the city, Tianhe encamped north of the city, and Sengming and Wenyu separately occupied the east and west; officials and people all responded to them.

sentences.zh: 一日之中，眾至數萬。

translations.literal: Within one day, the multitude reached several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Within one day, the multitude reached several tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝時在高要，聞事起，率眾來討，大破之，殺天合，禽僧明及文育等，並釋之，引為主帥。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Chen was then at Gaoyao; when he heard that the affair had arisen, he led troops to attack, defeated them badly, killed Tianhe, captured Sengming, Wenyu, and the others, then released them all and appointed them as chief commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Chen was then at Gaoyao; when he heard that the affair had arisen, he led troops to attack, defeated them badly, killed Tianhe, captured Sengming, Wenyu, and the others, then released them all and appointed them as chief commanders.

sentences.zh: 武帝征交阯及討元景仲，僧明、文育並有功。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu campaigned against Jiaozhi and attacked Yuan Jingzhong, Sengming and Wenyu both had merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu campaigned against Jiaozhi and attacked Yuan Jingzhong, Sengming and Wenyu both had merit.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，俱隨武帝入援建鄴。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion, both followed the Emperor in marching to relieve Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, they both followed the Emperor north to relieve Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 武帝于始興破蘭裕，僧明為前鋒，斬裕。

translations.literal: When the Emperor defeated Lan Yu at Shixing, Sengming served as vanguard and beheaded Yu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor routed Lan Yu at Shixing, Sengming led the van and killed Yu with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 又與蔡路養戰于南野，僧明馬被傷，武帝馳救之，以所乘馬授僧明。

translations.literal: He also fought Cai Luyang at Nanye; Sengming's horse was wounded, and the Emperor galloped to his rescue and gave him the horse he himself was riding.
translations.idiomatic: In another battle with Cai Luyang at Nanye, Sengming's mount was struck down; the Emperor rode to his aid and gave him his own horse.

sentences.zh: 僧明上馬復進，殺數十人，因而乘之，大敗路養。

translations.literal: Sengming mounted again and pressed forward, killing several tens of men; riding on this momentum, he routed Luyang utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Sengming remounted, cut down dozens of the enemy, and pressing the advantage, won a crushing victory over Luyang.

sentences.zh: 高州刺史李遷仕又據大皋，入灨石，以逼武帝。

translations.literal: Li Qianshi, inspector of Gaozhou, again seized Dago, entered Ganshi, and pressed upon the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qianshi of Gaozhou again held Dago, advanced into Ganshi, and threatened the Emperor's position.

sentences.zh: 武帝遣周文育為前軍，與僧明擊走之。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Zhou Wenyu as vanguard; together with Sengming he drove Qianshi off.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Zhou Wenyu ahead with Sengming, and together they drove Qianshi back.

sentences.zh: 遷仕與甯都人劉孝尚並力將襲南康，陳武又令僧明與文育等拒之。

translations.literal: Qianshi and Liu Xiaoshang of Ningdu combined their forces and were about to strike Nankang; Chen Wu again ordered Sengming and Wenyu and others to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Qianshi joined with Liu Xiaoshang of Ningdu to attack Nankang; Chen Baxian once more sent Sengming, Wenyu, and the rest to hold them off.

sentences.zh: 相持連戰百餘日，卒禽遷仕，送于武帝。

translations.literal: They faced each other in battle for more than a hundred days in succession and finally captured Qianshi alive and sent him to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a hundred days of fighting, they took Qianshi alive and delivered him to the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 及帝下南康，留僧明頓西昌，督安成、廬陵二郡軍事。

translations.literal: When the Emperor descended on Nankang, he left Sengming stationed at Xichang to supervise military affairs in the two commanderies of Ancheng and Luling.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor moved on Nankang, he left Sengming at Xichang to oversee the armies of Ancheng and Luling.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝承制，授新州刺史、臨江縣子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed the regency, he appointed him inspector of Xinzhou and Viscount of Linjiang county.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang, acting as regent, made him inspector of Xinzhou and Viscount of Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 侯景遣于慶等寇南江，武帝頓豫章，命僧明為前驅，所向克捷。

translations.literal: Hou Jing sent Yu Qing and others to invade Nanjiang; Emperor Wu halted at Yuzhang and ordered Sengming to serve as vanguard, and wherever he went he won victories.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing sent Yu Qing and others to invade Nanjiang; Emperor Wu halted at Yuzhang and ordered Sengming to serve as vanguard, and wherever he went he won victories.

sentences.zh: 武帝表僧明為長史，仍隨東討。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu memorialized to make Sengming chief clerk, and Sengming then followed him eastward in campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu memorialized to make Sengming chief clerk, and Sengming then followed him eastward in campaign.

sentences.zh: 軍至蔡洲，僧明率麾下燒賊水門大艦。

translations.literal: When the army reached Caizhou, Sengming led his subordinates in burning the rebels’ great warships at the water gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Caizhou, Sengming led his subordinates in burning the rebels’ great warships at the water gate.

sentences.zh: 及景平，除南兗州刺史，進爵為侯，仍領晉陵太守。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified, Sengming was appointed inspector of Southern Yanzhou, advanced in noble rank to marquis, and still concurrently served as governor of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing was pacified, Sengming was appointed inspector of Southern Yanzhou, advanced in noble rank to marquis, and still concurrently served as governor of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 及荊州覆亡，武帝使僧明率吳明徹等隨侯瑱西援，於江州病卒。

translations.literal: When Jingzhou fell, Emperor Wu had Sengming lead Wu Mingche and others to follow Hou Tian westward in relief, but Sengming fell ill and died in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzhou fell, Emperor Wu had Sengming lead Wu Mingche and others to follow Hou Tian westward in relief, but Sengming fell ill and died in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍，諡曰威。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the office of Regular Mounted Attendant, and his posthumous title was Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the office of Regular Mounted Attendant, and his posthumous title was Wei.

sentences.zh: 陳文帝即位，追贈開府儀同三司，配享武帝廟庭。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Chen took the throne, Sengming was posthumously granted Kaifu Yitong Sansi and was enshrined in attendance in Emperor Wu’s ancestral temple court.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Chen took the throne, Sengming was posthumously granted Kaifu Yitong Sansi and was enshrined in attendance in Emperor Wu’s ancestral temple court.

sentences.zh: 子晉嗣。

translations.literal: His son Jin succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jin succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 周文育字景德，義興陽羨人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Wenyu, courtesy name Jingde, was a native of Yangxian in Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wenyu, styled Jingde, came from Yangxian in Yixing commandery.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，本居新安壽昌縣，姓項氏，名猛奴。

translations.literal: Orphaned and poor in youth, he originally lived in Shouchang county in Xin'an; his surname was Xiang and his name Mengnu.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his parents early and grew up in poverty in Shouchang, Xin'an, where he was known by the surname Xiang and the name Mengnu.

sentences.zh: 年十一，能反復游水中數里，跳高六尺，與群兒聚戲，眾莫能及。

translations.literal: At eleven he could swim back and forth in the water for several li, leap six feet in height, and when he gathered with the other boys to play, none could match him.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven he could swim several li without tiring, leap six feet from a standstill, and outplay every boy in the neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 義興人周薈為壽昌浦口戍主，見而奇之，因召與語。

translations.literal: Zhou Hui of Yixing was garrison commander at Shouchang Pukou; seeing the boy, he marveled at him and summoned him to talk.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Hui of Yixing, commander of the Shouchang river post, was struck by the boy and called him over to speak with him.

sentences.zh: 文育對曰：「母老家貧，兄弟姊並長大，困於賦役。」

translations.literal: Wenyu answered, "My mother is old, our house is poor, and my brothers and sisters are all grown; taxes and labor service are ruining us."
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu answered, "My mother is old, our house is poor, and my brothers and sisters are all grown; taxes and labor service are ruining us."

sentences.zh: 薈哀之，乃隨文育至家，就其母請文育養為己子，母遂與之。

translations.literal: Hui took pity on him, followed Wenyu home, and asked his mother to let him adopt Wenyu as his son; the mother then gave him up.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, Hui went home with Wenyu and asked his mother to let him adopt the boy; she agreed and released him to Hui's care.

sentences.zh: 及薈秩滿，與文育還都，見太子詹事周舍，請制名字，舍因為立名為文育，字景德。

translations.literal: When Hui's term of office expired, he returned to the capital with Wenyu, saw the Crown Prince's household steward Zhou She, and asked him to devise a formal name; She thereupon gave him the name Wenyu and the courtesy name Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui's tour ended, he brought Wenyu to the capital and asked Zhou She, steward to the crown prince, for a proper name; She named him Wenyu and gave him the style Jingde.

sentences.zh: 命兄子弘讓教之書計。

translations.literal: He ordered his nephew Hongrang to teach him writing and reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: He had his nephew Hongrang teach him letters and accounts.

sentences.zh: 弘讓善隸書，寫蔡邕勸學及古詩以遺之，文育不之省，謂弘讓曰：「誰能學此，取富貴但有大槊耳。」

translations.literal: Hongrang, a fine calligrapher, copied out Cai Yong's Exhortation to Learning and old poems for him, but Wenyu ignored them and said to Hongrang, "Who can study this? To gain wealth and rank, there is only the great lance."
translations.idiomatic: Hongrang, a fine calligrapher, copied out Cai Yong's Exhortation to Learning and old poems for him, but Wenyu ignored them and said to Hongrang, "Who can study this? To gain wealth and rank, there is only the great lance."

sentences.zh: 弘讓壯之，教之騎射，文育大悅。

translations.literal: Hongrang admired his spirit and taught him horsemanship and archery; Wenyu was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Impressed, Hongrang taught him riding and archery instead, to Wenyu's delight.

sentences.zh: 司州刺史陳慶之與薈同郡，素相善，啟薈為前軍軍主。

translations.literal: Chen Qingzhi, inspector of Sizhou, was from the same commandery as Hui and had long been on good terms with him; he recommended Hui as commander of the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qingzhi of Sizhou, a fellow townsman and old friend of Hui's, had him appointed commander of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 慶之使薈將五百人往新蔡懸瓠慰勞白水蠻。

translations.literal: Qingzhi sent Hui with five hundred men to Xincai and Xuanhuo to comfort and reward the Baishui barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi sent Hui with five hundred men to Xincai and Xuanhuo to pacify the Baishui tribes.

sentences.zh: 蠻謀執薈以入魏，事覺，薈與文育拒之。

translations.literal: The barbarians plotted to seize Hui and deliver him to Wei; when the plot was discovered, Hui and Wenyu resisted them.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes plotted to capture Hui and hand him to Wei; when the plot came out, Hui and Wenyu fought them off.

sentences.zh: 時賊徒甚盛，一日中戰數十合，文育前鋒陷陣，勇冠軍中。

translations.literal: The rebels were then very strong; in a single day they fought several tens of engagements, and Wenyu as vanguard broke the enemy lines—his valor was foremost in the army.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy was overwhelming; they clashed dozens of times in one day, and Wenyu, leading the van, broke their ranks—none in the army fought more fiercely.

sentences.zh: 薈于陣戰死，文育馳取其屍，賊不敢逼。

translations.literal: Hui was killed in battle; Wenyu galloped in and recovered his body, and the rebels did not dare press him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui fell in the fighting; Wenyu rode in under fire, recovered his body, and the enemy dared not close on him.

sentences.zh: 及夕，各引去。

translations.literal: By evening each side withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk both sides drew off.

sentences.zh: 文育身被九創，創愈，辭請還葬，慶之壯其節，厚加賵遺而遣之。

translations.literal: Wenyu's body bore nine wounds; when the wounds healed he asked leave to return and bury Hui; Qingzhi admired his loyalty, gave him generous funeral gifts, and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu had taken nine wounds; once healed he asked to go home and bury Hui. Qingzhi honored his devotion, gave him rich gifts for the funeral, and let him go.

sentences.zh: 葬訖，會盧安興為南江督護，啟文育同行。

translations.literal: When the burial was finished, it happened that Lu Anxing became protector of Nanjiang and asked Wenyu to go with him.
translations.idiomatic: After the funeral, Lu Anxing became protector of the southern rivers and invited Wenyu to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 累征有功，除南海令。

translations.literal: In repeated campaigns he won merit and was appointed magistrate of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: He earned distinction in campaign after campaign and was made magistrate of Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 安興死後，文育與杜僧明攻廣州，為陳武帝所敗，帝赦之。

translations.literal: After Anxing died, Wenyu and Du Sengming attacked Guangzhou, were defeated by Chen the Emperor, and the Emperor pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: After Anxing's death, Wenyu and Du Sengming attacked Guangzhou, were beaten by Chen Baxian, and were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 後監州王勱以文育為長流，深被委任。

translations.literal: Later the supervising inspector Wang Mai made Wenyu his chief adjutant and entrusted him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Mai, inspector of the region, made Wenyu his chief adjutant and relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 勱被代，文育欲與勱俱下。

translations.literal: When Mai was replaced, Wenyu wished to go downriver with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Mai was relieved of his post, Wenyu wanted to leave with him for the north.

sentences.zh: 至大庾嶺，詣卜者，卜者曰：「君北下不過作令長，南入則為公侯。」

translations.literal: At Dayu Pass he consulted a fortune-teller, who said, "If you go north, you will be no more than a county magistrate; if you enter the south, you will become a duke or marquis."
translations.idiomatic: At Dayu Pass he consulted a fortune-teller, who said, "If you go north, you will be no more than a county magistrate; if you enter the south, you will become a duke or marquis."

sentences.zh: 文育曰：「足錢便可，誰望公侯。」

translations.literal: Wenyu said, "Enough money is fine—who aspires to be duke or marquis?"
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu replied, "Enough silver will do—who dreams of titles?"

sentences.zh: 卜人又曰：「君須臾當暴得銀至二千兩，若不見信，以此為驗。」

translations.literal: The diviner added, "You will presently gain silver all at once, up to two thousand taels; if you do not believe it, take this as proof."
translations.idiomatic: The diviner added, "You will soon come by two thousand taels of silver in a single stroke—take that as proof if you doubt me."

sentences.zh: 其夕，宿逆旅，有賈人求與文育博，文育勝之，得銀二千兩。

translations.literal: That evening he lodged at an inn; a merchant asked to gamble with Wenyu, Wenyu won, and gained two thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: That night at an inn a trader challenged him to dice; Wenyu won exactly two thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 旦辭勱，勱問其故，文育以告，勱乃遣之。

translations.literal: At dawn he took leave of Mai; Mai asked the reason, Wenyu told him, and Mai then sent him on.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he told Mai he was leaving; when Mai heard why, he let him go south.

sentences.zh: 武帝聞其還，大喜，分麾下配焉。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of his return he was greatly pleased and assigned men from his own following to him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was delighted when he heard Wenyu had returned and gave him troops from his own guard.

sentences.zh: 武帝之討侯景，文育與杜僧明為前軍，克蘭裕，援歐陽頠，皆有功。

translations.literal: In the Emperor's campaign against Hou Jing, Wenyu and Du Sengming served as vanguard, defeated Lan Yu, and relieved Ouyang Wei—all with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the war against Hou Jing, Wenyu and Du Sengming led the van, defeated Lan Yu, and relieved Ouyang Wei, earning credit in each action.

sentences.zh: 武帝破蔡路養于南野，文育為路養所圍，四面數重，矢石雨下，所乘馬死，文育右手搏戰，左手解鞍，潰圍而出。

translations.literal: When the Emperor defeated Cai Luyang at Nanye, Wenyu was surrounded by Luyang, ringed on all sides several ranks deep, with arrows and stones raining down; the horse he rode was killed, but Wenyu fought with his right hand while undoing the saddle with his left and broke out of the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: At Nanye the Emperor routed Cai Luyang, but Wenyu was trapped in rings of enemy troops under a hail of missiles; his horse was killed, yet fighting with one hand and stripping the saddle with the other he broke free.

sentences.zh: 與杜僧明等相得，並力復進，遂大敗之。

translations.literal: He joined up with Du Sengming and the others, advanced together with combined strength, and utterly defeated the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He rejoined Du Sengming and the rest, and together they counterattacked and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 武帝乃表文育為府司馬。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon memorialized that Wenyu be appointed headquarters marshal.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then recommended him as marshal of his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 李遷仕之據大皋，遣其將軍杜平虜入灨石魚梁作城。

translations.literal: When Li Qianshi held Dago, he sent his general Du Pinglu into Ganshi at Yuliang to build a fort.
translations.idiomatic: While Li Qianshi held Dago, he sent Du Pinglu to build a fort at Yuliang in Ganshi.

sentences.zh: 武帝命文育擊之，平虜棄城走，文育據其城。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Wenyu to attack; Pinglu abandoned the city and fled, and Wenyu seized it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Wenyu against him; Pinglu abandoned the fort and fled, and Wenyu occupied it.

sentences.zh: 遷仕聞平虜敗，留老弱於大皋，悉選精兵自將以攻文育。

translations.literal: When Qianshi heard that Pinglu had been defeated, he left the old and weak at Dago, chose all his picked troops, and personally led them to attack Wenyu.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Pinglu's defeat, Qianshi left the weak at Dago and led his best troops against Wenyu in person.

sentences.zh: 文育與戰，遷仕稍卻，相持未解。

translations.literal: Wenyu fought him; Qianshi fell back slightly, and the two sides remained locked in stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu met him in battle; Qianshi gave ground little by little, and the fight hung in the balance.

sentences.zh: 會武帝遣杜僧明來援，別破遷仕水軍，遷仕眾潰，不敢過大皋，直走新淦。

translations.literal: Just then the Emperor sent Du Sengming to reinforce him; on another front he routed Qianshi's river forces, Qianshi's host collapsed, and he did not dare pass Dago but fled straight to Xingan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then sent Du Sengming, who smashed Qianshi's fleet; Qianshi's army broke and he fled past Dago straight to Xingan.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝授文育義州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang appointed Wenyu inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang made him inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 遷仕又與劉孝尚謀拒義軍，武帝遣文育與侯安都、杜僧明、徐度、杜棱築城於白口拒之。

translations.literal: Qianshi again plotted with Liu Xiaoshang to resist the loyalist army; the Emperor sent Wenyu with Hou Andou, Du Sengming, Xu Du, and Du Leng to build a fort at Baikou and hold them off.
translations.idiomatic: Qianshi joined Liu Xiaoshang to block the loyalist advance; the Emperor sent Wenyu, Hou Andou, Du Sengming, Xu Du, and Du Leng to fortify Baikou and stop them.

sentences.zh: 文育頻出與戰，遂禽遷仕。

translations.literal: Wenyu sallied forth repeatedly to fight and finally captured Qianshi alive.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu fought them again and again until he took Qianshi alive.

sentences.zh: 武帝發自南康，遣文育將兵五千，開通江路。

translations.literal: The Emperor set out from Nankang and sent Wenyu with five thousand troops to open the Jiang route.
translations.idiomatic: Marching from Nankang, the Emperor sent Wenyu with five thousand men to clear the river road.

sentences.zh: 侯景將王伯醜據豫章，文育擊走之，遂據其城。

translations.literal: Wang Bichou, a general of Hou Jing, held Yuzhang; Wenyu attacked and drove him off, then seized the city.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing's officer Wang Bichou held Yuzhang; Wenyu drove him out and took the city.

sentences.zh: 累功封東遷縣侯。

translations.literal: For accumulated merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongqian county.
translations.idiomatic: His accumulated merit won him the marquisate of Dongqian.

sentences.zh: 武帝軍至白茅灣，命文育與杜僧明常為軍鋒。

translations.literal: When the Emperor's army reached Baimao Bay, he ordered Wenyu and Du Sengming to serve regularly as the army's spearhead.
translations.idiomatic: At Baimao Bay the Emperor made Wenyu and Du Sengming his usual shock troops.

sentences.zh: 及至姑孰，與侯景將侯子鑒戰，破之。

translations.literal: When they reached Gushu, he fought Hou Jing's general Hou Zijian and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: At Gushu he met Hou Jing's general Hou Zijian and routed him.

sentences.zh: 景平，改封南移縣侯，累遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified, his fief was changed to Marquis of Nanyi county, and he was promoted in succession to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing's fall his fief was changed to Nanyi, and he rose to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 武帝誅王僧辯，令文育督眾軍，會文帝于吳興，圍克杜龕。

translations.literal: When the Emperor executed Wang Senbian, he ordered Wenyu to command the armies, join the Prince of Jin at Wuxing, and besiege and capture Du Kan.
translations.idiomatic: After the Emperor killed Wang Senbian, he put Wenyu in command of the armies to join Chen Qian at Wuxing and take Du Kan by siege.

sentences.zh: 又濟江襲會稽太守張彪，得其郡城。

translations.literal: He also crossed the river, raided Zhang Biao, administrator of Kuaiji, and took the commandery city.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the river, surprised Kuaiji administrator Zhang Biao, and seized the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 及文帝為彪所襲，文育時頓城北香岩寺，文帝夜往趨之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin was attacked by Biao, Wenyu was then stationed at Xiangyan Temple north of the city; the prince went to him by night in haste.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Qian was ambushed by Biao, Wenyu was at Xiangyan Temple north of the city; Chen Qian rode to him by night.

sentences.zh: 彪又來攻，文育苦戰，遂破平彪。

translations.literal: Biao attacked again; Wenyu fought bitterly and finally defeated and pacified Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Biao attacked again; after a hard fight Wenyu destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 武帝以侯瑱擁據江州，命文育討之，仍除南豫州刺史，率兵襲盆城。

translations.literal: Because Hou Zhen held Jiangzhou by force, the Emperor ordered Wenyu to suppress him, and at the same time appointed him inspector of South Yuzhou and led troops to storm Pencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Zhen held Jiangzhou; the Emperor sent Wenyu against him, made him inspector of South Yuzhou, and had him strike at Pencheng.

sentences.zh: 未克，徐嗣徽引齊人度江，據蕪湖，詔徵文育還都。

translations.literal: Before he could take it, Xu Sihui brought Qi troops across the river and seized Wuhu; an edict recalled Wenyu to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before the city fell, Xu Sihui brought Northern Qi troops across the Yangtze and seized Wuhu; Wenyu was ordered back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 嗣徽等乃列艦於青墩至於七磯，以斷文育歸路。

translations.literal: Sihui and the others then lined up their ships from Qingdun to Qiji to cut off Wenyu's line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Sihui blocked the river from Qingdun to Qiji with his fleet to cut off Wenyu's retreat.

sentences.zh: 及夕，文育鼓噪而發，嗣徽等不能制。

translations.literal: At evening Wenyu set out with drums and shouts; Sihui and the others could not stop him.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Wenyu broke out with a great clamor of drums; Sihui could not hold him.

sentences.zh: 至旦，反攻嗣徽，嗣徽驍將鮑砰獨以小艦殿，文育乘單舴艋，跳入砰艦，斬砰，仍牽其艦而還，賊眾大駭。

translations.literal: By dawn he counterattacked Sihui; Sihui's fierce general Bao Peng alone brought up the rear in a small vessel. Wenyu boarded a single skiff, leaped into Peng's ship, beheaded Peng, then towed the vessel back—the rebel host was greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he turned on Sihui; Sihui's champion Bao Peng covered the retreat in a light boat. Wenyu took a skiff alone, boarded Peng's ship, killed him, and towed the boat back—the enemy was stunned.

sentences.zh: 因留船蕪湖，自丹陽步上。

translations.literal: He then left his boats at Wuhu and went up by land from Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He left his ships at Wuhu and marched overland from Danyang.

sentences.zh: 時武帝拒嗣徽于白城，適與文育會。

translations.literal: The Emperor was then holding Sihui off at Baicheng and happened to join Wenyu.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was holding Sihui at Baicheng and met Wenyu just in time.

sentences.zh: 將戰，風急，武帝曰：「矢不逆風。」

translations.literal: As they were about to fight, the wind was fierce, and Emperor Wu said, "Arrows cannot be shot against the wind."
translations.idiomatic: As they were about to fight, the wind was fierce, and Emperor Wu said, "Arrows cannot be shot against the wind."

sentences.zh: 文育曰：「事急矣，當決之，何用古法。」

translations.literal: Wenyu said, "The matter is urgent—we must decide it now; what use is the old rule?"
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu replied, "This is urgent—we must fight now, not wait on custom."

sentences.zh: 抽槊上馬而進，眾軍隨之，風亦尋轉，殺傷數百人。

translations.literal: He drew his spear, mounted, and advanced; the whole army followed, the wind soon shifted, and several hundred were killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: He seized his spear, mounted, and charged; the army followed, the wind shifted, and hundreds fell on both sides.

sentences.zh: 嗣徽等移營莫府山，文育徙頓對之。

translations.literal: Sihui and the others moved camp to Mofu Mountain; Wenyu shifted his station to face them.
translations.idiomatic: Sihui withdrew to Mofu Mountain; Wenyu moved his camp to confront him.

sentences.zh: 頻戰功最，進爵壽昌縣公，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: In repeated battles his merit was foremost; he was advanced to Duke of Shouchang county and granted one set of martial pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: His merit in the fighting was greatest; he was made Duke of Shouchang and given a band of martial music.

sentences.zh: 及廣州刺史蕭勃舉兵踰嶺，詔文育督眾軍討之。

translations.literal: When Xiao Bo, inspector of Guangzhou, raised troops and crossed the ridge, an edict ordered Wenyu to command the armies in suppressing him.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzhou inspector Xiao Bo rebelled and crossed the mountains, Wenyu was put in command of the forces sent against him.

sentences.zh: 時新吳洞主餘孝頃舉兵應勃，遣其弟孝勱守郡城，自出豫章，據於石頭。

translations.literal: At that time Yu Xiaodun, cave lord of Xinwu, raised troops in support of Bo, sent his younger brother Xiaoli to hold the commandery city, and himself went out to Yuzhang and seized Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xiaodun of Xinwu joined Bo, left his brother Xiaoli to hold the prefectural seat, and took Shitou from Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 勃使其子孜將兵與孝頃相會，又遣其別將歐陽頠頓軍苦竹灘，傅泰據墌口城，以拒官軍。

translations.literal: Bo sent his son Zi with troops to join Xiaodun, and also sent his separate commander Ouyang Wei to encamp at Kuzhu Ford while Fu Tai held Yikou city to resist the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: Bo sent his son Zi to join Xiaodun, posted Ouyang Wei at Kuzhu Ford, and put Fu Tai in Yikou to block the government forces.

sentences.zh: 官軍船少，孝頃有舴艋三百艘、艦百餘乘在上牢，文育遣軍主焦僧度、羊柬潛軍襲之，悉取而歸，仍于豫章立柵。

translations.literal: The imperial army had few ships; Xiaodun had three hundred skiffs and more than a hundred war vessels at Shanglao. Wenyu sent the commanders Jiao Songdu and Yang Jian with a hidden force to raid them, took them all, and then built a stockade at Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Government forces were short of boats while Xiaodun had three hundred skiffs and a hundred warships at Shanglao; Wenyu sent Jiao Songdu and Yang Jian on a night raid, captured the whole fleet, and built a camp at Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 時官軍食盡，欲退還，文育不許。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial army's provisions were exhausted and they wished to withdraw; Wenyu would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Government rations ran out and the army wanted to pull back; Wenyu refused.

sentences.zh: 乃使人間行，遺周迪書，約為兄弟，並陳利害。

translations.literal: He then sent men by secret paths with a letter to Zhou Di, proposing brotherhood and setting forth advantage and harm.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys by hidden routes to Zhou Di, offering alliance as brothers and explaining what each side stood to gain or lose.

sentences.zh: 迪得書甚喜，許饋以糧。

translations.literal: When Di received the letter he was greatly pleased and promised to supply grain.
translations.idiomatic: Di was delighted and promised to send food.

sentences.zh: 於是文育分遣老小，乘故船舫沿流俱下，燒豫章所立柵，偽退，孝頃望之大喜，因不設備。

translations.literal: Wenyu then sent off the old and young separately; they boarded the old boats and went downstream together, burned the stockade built at Yuzhang, and feigned retreat. Xiaodun saw this from afar and was greatly pleased, and therefore made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu sent women and children downriver on the old boats, burned the Yuzhang camp, and pretended to retreat; Xiaodun watched with joy and let his guard down.

sentences.zh: 文育由間道信宿達芊韶。

translations.literal: Wenyu traveled two nights by hidden paths and reached Qianshao.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu marched two days by back trails and reached Qianshao.

sentences.zh: 芊韶上流則歐陽頠、蕭勃，下流則傅泰、餘孝頃，文育據其中間，築城饗士，賊徒大駭。

translations.literal: Upstream at Qianshao were Ouyang Wei and Xiao Bo; downstream were Fu Tai and Yu Xiaodun. Wenyu seized the ground between, built a city, and feasted his troops—the rebel bands were greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Wei and Xiao Bo lay above Qianshao, Fu Tai and Yu Xiaodun below; Wenyu camped between them, fortified the place, and feasted his men—the rebels were thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 歐陽頠乃退入泥溪，作城自守。

translations.literal: Ouyang Wei then withdrew into Nixi, built a fort, and held it.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Wei fell back to Nixi and walled himself in.

sentences.zh: 文育遣嚴威將軍周鐵武與長史陸山才襲頠，禽之。

translations.literal: Wenyu sent the Strictly Martial General Zhou Tiewu and his chief clerk Lu Shancai to raid Wei and captured him alive.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu sent Zhou Tiewu and chief clerk Lu Shancai against him and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 於是盛陳兵甲，與頠乘舟而宴，以巡傅泰城下，因攻泰，克之。

translations.literal: He then arrayed arms and armor in full display, feasted with Wei aboard a boat, and sailed past Fu Tai's city to inspect it; he then attacked Tai and took the place.
translations.idiomatic: He paraded his troops, feasted with Wei on the river, sailed past Fu Tai's walls, then stormed the city and took it.

sentences.zh: 蕭勃在南康，聞之，眾皆股栗。

translations.literal: Xiao Bo was at Nankang; when he heard of this, all his followers trembled in their thighs.
translations.idiomatic: At Nankang, Xiao Bo's men shook with fear when they heard the news.

sentences.zh: 其將譚世遠斬勃欲降，為人所害。

translations.literal: His general Tan Shiyuan beheaded Bo intending to surrender, but was killed by someone.
translations.idiomatic: His officer Tan Shiyuan killed Bo to surrender, but was slain before he could deliver the head.

sentences.zh: 世遠軍主夏侯明徹持勃首以降。

translations.literal: Shiyuan's army commander Xiahou Mingche brought Bo's head and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Shiyuan's subordinate Xiahou Mingche brought Bo's head and submitted.

sentences.zh: 蕭孜、餘孝頃猶據石頭，武帝遣侯安都助文育攻之，孜降文育，孝頃退走新吳，廣州平。

translations.literal: Xiao Zi and Yu Xiaodun still held Shitou; the Emperor sent Hou Andou to assist Wenyu in attacking them. Zi surrendered to Wenyu, Xiaodun fled to Xinwu, and Guangzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zi and Yu Xiaodun still held Shitou; the Emperor sent Hou Andou to help Wenyu. Zi surrendered, Xiaodun fled to Xinwu, and the Guangzhou rebellion was over.

sentences.zh: 文育還頓豫章，以功授開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Wenyu returned and stationed at Yuzhang; for his merit he was appointed Grand Master with the same privileges as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu returned to Yuzhang and, for his merit, was made Grand Master with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 王琳擁據上流，詔侯安都為西道都督，文育為南道都督，同會武昌。

translations.literal: Wang Lin held the upper reaches of the river; an edict made Hou Andou commander of the western route and Wenyu commander of the southern route, to meet at Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin held the upper Yangtze; Hou Andou was made western commander and Wenyu southern commander, with orders to join at Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 與琳戰於沌口，為琳所執，後得逃歸，請罪，詔不問，復其官爵。

translations.literal: He fought Lin at Zhunkou, was captured by Lin, later escaped and returned, asked to be punished, but an edict took no notice and restored his office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Wang Lin at Zhunkou, was captured, later escaped, and asked to be punished; the Emperor pardoned him and restored his titles.

sentences.zh: 及周迪破餘孝頃，孝頃子公揚、弟孝勱猶據舊柵，擾動南土，武帝復遣文育及周迪、黃法奭等討之。

translations.literal: When Zhou Di defeated Yu Xiaodun, Xiaodun's son Gongyang and younger brother Xiaoli still held the old stockades and disturbed the southern lands; the Emperor again sent Wenyu with Zhou Di, Huang Fa, and others to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou Di broke Yu Xiaodun, Xiaodun's son Gongyang and brother Xiaoli still held the old forts and troubled the south; the Emperor sent Wenyu, Zhou Di, Huang Fa, and the rest against them.

sentences.zh: 豫章內史熊曇朗亦率眾來會。

translations.literal: Xiong Tanlang, interior minister of Yuzhang, also led his forces to join the assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Tanlang, interior minister of Yuzhang, brought his troops to join them.

sentences.zh: 文育遣吳明徹為水軍，配周迪運糧，自率眾軍入象牙江，築城于金口。

translations.literal: Wenyu sent Wu Mingche as river commander, assigned Zhou Di to transport grain, and himself led the main army into Ivory River and built a fort at Jinkou.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu put Wu Mingche in charge of the fleet, set Zhou Di to convoy grain, and led the main force up Ivory River to fortify Jinkou.

sentences.zh: 公揚偽降，謀執文育，事覺，文育囚之送都，以其部曲分隸眾軍。

translations.literal: Gongyang feigned surrender and plotted to seize Wenyu; when the plot was discovered, Wenyu imprisoned him and sent him to the capital, dividing his followers among the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyang pretended to submit and plotted to capture Wenyu; when the plot was exposed, Wenyu sent him to the capital in chains and drafted his men into other units.

sentences.zh: 乃舍舟為步軍，進據三陂。

translations.literal: He then abandoned the boats and became an infantry force, advancing to hold Sanpi.
translations.idiomatic: He then left the river, marched as infantry, and seized Sanpi.

sentences.zh: 王琳遣將曹慶救孝勱，分遣主帥常眾愛與文育相拒，自帥所領攻周迪、吳明徹軍。

translations.literal: Wang Lin sent his general Cao Qing to rescue Xiaoli, dispatched his commander Chang Zhong'ai to hold Wenyu off, and personally led his own troops to attack the armies of Zhou Di and Wu Mingche.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin sent Cao Qing to relieve Xiaoli, posted Chang Zhong'ai against Wenyu, and led his main force against Zhou Di and Wu Mingche.

sentences.zh: 迪等敗，文育退據金口。

translations.literal: Di and the others were defeated, and Wenyu withdrew to hold Jinkou.
translations.idiomatic: Di was beaten and Wenyu fell back to Jinkou.

sentences.zh: 熊曇朗因其失利，謀害文育以應眾愛。

translations.literal: Xiong Tanlang, taking advantage of this setback, plotted to kill Wenyu in order to join Zhong'ai.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Wenyu's defeat, Xiong Tanlang plotted to kill him and go over to Zhong'ai.

sentences.zh: 文育監軍孫白象頗知其事，勸令先之。

translations.literal: Wenyu's army supervisor Sun Baixiang learned of the matter and urged him to strike first.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu's supervisor Sun Baixiang learned of the plot and urged a preemptive strike.

sentences.zh: 文育曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Wenyu said, "That will not do.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu said, "No.

sentences.zh: 我舊兵少，客軍多，若取曇朗，人皆驚懼，亡立至矣，不如推心撫之。」

translations.literal: My old troops are few and guest troops many; if I seize Tanlang, everyone will be frightened, and flight will come at once. It is better to treat him with open trust."
translations.idiomatic: My old troops are few and guest troops many; if I seize Tanlang, everyone will be frightened, and flight will come at once. It is better to treat him with open trust."

sentences.zh: 初，周迪之敗，棄船走，莫知所在。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhou Di was defeated, he abandoned his boats and fled, and no one knew where he had gone.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Di had been beaten earlier, he abandoned his fleet and vanished.

sentences.zh: 及得迪書，文育喜，齎示曇朗，曇朗害之於坐。

translations.literal: When he received a letter from Di, Wenyu rejoiced and brought it to show Tanlang; Tanlang killed him at the feast.
translations.idiomatic: When a letter came from Di, Wenyu rejoiced and showed it to Tanlang, who killed him at table.

sentences.zh: 武帝聞之，即日舉哀，贈侍中、司空，諡曰忠湣。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of it he mourned the same day, posthumously appointed him Palace Attendant and Minister of Works, and gave him the posthumous title Loyal and Lamented.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor mourned him the same day, posthumously made him Palace Attendant and Minister of Works, and gave him the posthumous name Zhongmin, Loyal and Lamented.

sentences.zh: 初文育之據三陂，有流星墜地，其聲如雷，地陷方一丈，中有碎炭數斗。

translations.literal: When Wenyu first held Sanpi, a meteor fell to earth with a sound like thunder; the ground sank to a square of one zhang, and within it were several dou of broken charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: While Wenyu held Sanpi, a meteor crashed to earth like thunder, leaving a pit one zhang square filled with charred fragments.

sentences.zh: 又軍市中忽聞小兒啼，一市並驚，聽之在土下，軍人掘焉，得棺，長三尺，文育惡之。

translations.literal: Again in the army market a child's cry was suddenly heard; the whole market was alarmed, and listening, they traced it beneath the ground. Soldiers dug and found a coffin three feet long—Wenyu took it as an ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: In camp a child's wail was heard from underground; soldiers dug up a coffin three feet long, which Wenyu took as a bad sign.

sentences.zh: 俄而迪敗，文育見殺。

translations.literal: Before long Di was defeated and Wenyu was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Di was beaten and Wenyu was murdered.

sentences.zh: 天嘉二年，有詔配享武帝廟庭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng an edict ordered him a place in the sacrifices at the Emperor's ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiancheng an edict gave him a place in the temple of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 子寶安嗣。

translations.literal: His son Bao'an succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bao'an succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 文育本族兄景曜，因文育官至新安太守。

translations.literal: Wenyu's clansman elder brother Jingyao, through Wenyu's influence, reached the post of administrator of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu's kinsman Jingyao rose through his patronage to become administrator of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 寶安字安人，年十餘歲，便習騎射。

translations.literal: Bao'an, courtesy name Anren, in his teens already practiced riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Bao'an, styled Anren, learned riding and archery in his teens.

sentences.zh: 以貴公子驕蹇游逸，好狗馬，樂驅馳，靡衣偷食。

translations.literal: As a nobleman's son he was arrogant, willful, and dissolute, fond of dogs and horses, delighting in reckless riding, extravagant in dress and idle in eating.
translations.idiomatic: As a nobleman's heir he was arrogant and wild, devoted to hounds and horses, reckless in riding, and extravagant in dress and table.

sentences.zh: 文育之為晉陵，以征討不遑之郡，令寶安監知郡事，尤聚惡少年，武帝患之。

translations.literal: When Wenyu was assigned to Jinling but could not attend the commandery because of campaigns, he had Bao'an supervise its affairs; he especially gathered vicious youths, which troubled the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenyu was made governor of Jinling but could not leave the field, he left Bao'an in charge; the boy gathered rowdies, to the Emperor's dismay.

sentences.zh: 及文育西征敗績，縶于王琳，寶安便折節讀書，與士君子游，綏禦文育士卒，甚有威惠。

translations.literal: When Wenyu was defeated on the western campaign and held prisoner by Wang Lin, Bao'an at once reformed himself, took up study, associated with gentlemen, and pacified Wenyu's troops with great authority and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenyu was captured by Wang Lin on the western campaign, Bao'an reformed, took up books, kept company with scholars, and ruled his father's troops with firm kindness.

sentences.zh: 文育歸，復除吳興太守。

translations.literal: When Wenyu returned he was again appointed administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenyu came home he was again made governor of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 文育為熊曇朗所害，征寶安還，起為猛烈將軍，領其舊兵，仍令南討。

translations.literal: When Wenyu was killed by Xiong Tanlang, Bao'an was recalled, appointed Fierce General, given command of his father's old troops, and ordered south to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: After Wenyu was killed by Xiong Tanlang, Bao'an was recalled, made Fierce General, given his father's troops, and sent south.

sentences.zh: 文帝即位，深器重之，寄以心膂，精卒多配焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, he deeply valued Zhou Bao’an and entrusted him as a man of heart and backbone, assigning many elite soldiers to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, he deeply valued Zhou Bao’an and entrusted him as a man of heart and backbone, assigning many elite soldiers to him.

sentences.zh: 及平王琳，頗有功。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin was pacified, Bao’an had considerable merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lin was pacified, Bao’an had considerable merit.

sentences.zh: 周迪之破熊曇朗，寶安南入，窮其餘燼。

translations.literal: When Zhou Di defeated Xiong Tanlang, Bao’an entered southward and exhausted the remnants.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Di defeated Xiong Tanlang, Bao’an entered southward and exhausted the remnants.

sentences.zh: 天嘉二年，重拜吳興太守，襲封壽昌縣公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjia, he was again appointed governor of Wuxing and inherited the enfeoffment as Duke of Shouchang County.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianjia, he was again appointed governor of Wuxing and inherited the enfeoffment as Duke of Shouchang County.

sentences.zh: 三年，征留異，為侯安都前軍。

translations.literal: In the third year, during the campaign against Liu Yi, he served as Hou Andu’s vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, during the campaign against Liu Yi, he served as Hou Andu’s vanguard.

sentences.zh: 異平，除給事黃門侍郎、衛尉卿。

translations.literal: When Yi was pacified, Bao’an was appointed Palace Attendant Gentleman and Chamberlain for the Palace Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi was pacified, Bao’an was appointed Palace Attendant Gentleman and Chamberlain for the Palace Garrison.

sentences.zh: 再遷左衛將軍，領衛尉卿。

translations.literal: After further promotions he became General of the Left Guard, concurrently Chamberlain for the Palace Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: After further promotions he became General of the Left Guard, concurrently Chamberlain for the Palace Garrison.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰成。

translations.literal: When he died, his posthumous title was Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his posthumous title was Cheng.

sentences.zh: 子屻嗣，位晉陵、定遠二郡太守。

translations.literal: His son Zi succeeded and served as administrator of the two commanderies of Jinling and Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zi succeeded him and became governor of Jinling and Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 侯瑱字伯玉，巴西充國人也。

translations.literal: Hou Zhen, courtesy name Boyu, was a native of Chongguo in Baxi.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Zhen, styled Boyu, came from Chongguo in Baxi commandery.

sentences.zh: 父弘遠，累世為西蜀酋豪。

translations.literal: His father Hongyuan had for generations been a chieftain of western Shu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hongyuan's family had been chieftains in western Shu for generations.

sentences.zh: 蜀賊張文萼據白崖山，有眾萬人，梁益州刺史鄱陽王蕭範命弘遠討之，弘遠戰死。

translations.literal: The Shu bandit Zhang Wene held Baiya Mountain with a host of ten thousand; Xiao Fan, Prince of Poyang and inspector of Yizhou under Liang, ordered Hongyuan to suppress him, and Hongyuan died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Zhang Wene held Baiya Mountain with ten thousand men; Prince Xiao Fan of Poyang, inspector of Yizhou, sent Hongyuan against him, and Hongyuan was killed.

sentences.zh: 瑱固請復讎，每戰先鋒，遂斬文萼，由是知名。

translations.literal: Zhen repeatedly begged to avenge his father, led the van in every battle, and finally beheaded Wene—thereby becoming famous.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen begged to avenge his father, fought in the van each time, and finally killed Wene, winning fame.

sentences.zh: 因事范，範委以將帥之任。

translations.literal: He entered Fan's service, and Fan entrusted him with command.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Fan's service and was entrusted with military command.

sentences.zh: 山谷夷、獠不附者，並遣瑱征之。

translations.literal: All the Yi and Liao in the valleys who would not submit were sent against under Zhen's command.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to subdue every Yi and Liao tribe in the hills that would not submit.

sentences.zh: 累功授輕車府中兵參軍、晉康太守。

translations.literal: For accumulated merit he was appointed Army Adjutant of the Light Chariots Office and administrator of Jinkang.
translations.idiomatic: His accumulated merit won him the posts of army adjutant in the Light Chariots Office and governor of Jinkang.

sentences.zh: 范為雍州刺史，瑱除馮翊太守。

translations.literal: When Fan became inspector of Yongzhou, Zhen was appointed administrator of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan became inspector of Yongzhou, Zhen was made governor of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 範遷鎮合肥，瑱又隨之。

translations.literal: When Fan moved his headquarters to Hefei, Zhen followed him again.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan transferred to Hefei, Zhen went with him.

sentences.zh: 侯景圍臺城，範乃遣瑱輔其世子嗣入援都。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing besieged the capital, Fan sent Zhen to assist his heir Si in marching to relieve the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing besieged the capital, Fan sent Zhen to escort his heir Si to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，瑱、嗣同退還合肥。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Zhen and Si withdrew together to Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Zhen and Si retreated to Hefei together.

sentences.zh: 仍隨範徙鎮盆城。

translations.literal: He again followed Fan when Fan moved his headquarters to Pencheng.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Fan when Fan moved his base to Pencheng.

sentences.zh: 俄而範及嗣皆卒，瑱領其眾，依于豫章太守莊鐵。

translations.literal: Before long both Fan and Si died; Zhen took command of their forces and attached himself to Zhuang Tie, administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Fan and Si both died; Zhen took over their troops and placed himself under Yuzhang administrator Zhuang Tie.

sentences.zh: 鐵疑之，瑱懼不自安，詐引鐵謀事，因刃之，據豫章之地。

translations.literal: Tie was suspicious of him; Zhen, fearing for his safety, pretended to invite Tie to discuss affairs and killed him with a blade, then seized the territory of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Tie distrusted him; Zhen, uneasy, lured Tie to a meeting and killed him, seizing Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 後降于侯景將于慶。

translations.literal: Later he surrendered to Yu Qing, a general of Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He later submitted to Hou Jing's general Yu Qing.

sentences.zh: 慶送瑱于景，景以瑱與己同姓，托為宗族，待之甚厚。

translations.literal: Qing sent Zhen to Jing; Jing, because Zhen bore the same surname, claimed him as a clansman and treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Qing sent him to Hou Jing, who claimed kinship on the shared surname Hou and treated him lavishly.

sentences.zh: 留其妻子及弟為質，遣瑱隨慶平蠡南諸郡。

translations.literal: He kept Zhen's wife, children, and younger brother as hostages and sent Zhen with Qing to pacify the southern commanderies of Li.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing kept his wife, children, and brother as hostages and sent Zhen with Qing to pacify the southern Li region.

sentences.zh: 及景敗巴陵，景將宋子仙、任約等並為西軍所獲，瑱乃誅景党與以應義師，景亦誅其弟及妻子。

translations.literal: When Jing was defeated at Baling, Jing's generals Song Zixian, Ren Yue, and others were all captured by the western army; Zhen then executed Jing's partisans to join the loyalist forces, and Jing in turn executed Zhen's younger brother and wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing lost at Baling and his generals Song Zixian and Ren Yue were captured, Zhen killed Jing's followers and went over to the loyalists; Jing executed Zhen's brother and family in revenge.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝授瑱南兗州刺史、郫縣侯。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang appointed Zhen inspector of South Yanzhou and Marquis of Pi county.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang made him inspector of South Yanzhou and Marquis of Pi.

sentences.zh: 仍隨都督王僧辯討景，恒為前鋒。

translations.literal: He again followed the commander Wang Senbian in suppressing Jing and was constantly in the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He followed commander Wang Senbian against Hou Jing and always led the van.

sentences.zh: 既復台城，景奔吳郡，僧辯使瑱追景，大敗之于吳松江。

translations.literal: After the capital was recovered, Jing fled to Wu commandery; Senbian sent Zhen to pursue Jing and routed him utterly on the Wusong River.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was retaken, Hou Jing fled to Wu; Senbian sent Zhen in pursuit and crushed him on the Wusong River.

sentences.zh: 以功除南豫州刺史，鎮姑孰。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed inspector of South Yuzhou and stationed at Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made inspector of South Yuzhou with his seat at Gushu.

sentences.zh: 及齊遣郭元建出濡須，僧辯遣瑱扞之，大敗元建。

translations.literal: When Qi sent Guo Yuanjian out through Ruxu, Senbian sent Zhen to resist him and routed Yuanjian utterly.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi sent Guo Yuanjian through Ruxu, Senbian sent Zhen against him and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 魏攻荊州，王僧辯以瑱為前軍赴援，未至而魏克荊州。

translations.literal: When Wei attacked Jingzhou, Wang Senbian made Zhen vanguard to go to its relief, but before he arrived Wei had taken Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei attacked Jingzhou, Senbian sent Zhen ahead to relieve it, but Wei took the province before he arrived.

sentences.zh: 瑱頓九江，因衛晉安王還都。

translations.literal: Zhen halted at Jiujiang and escorted the Prince of Jin'an back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen halted at Jiujiang and escorted the Prince of Jin'an home to the capital.

sentences.zh: 承制以瑱為侍中、江州刺史，加都督，改封康樂縣公。

translations.literal: Acting under the regency he was appointed Palace Attendant and inspector of Jiangzhou with added command authority, and his fief was changed to Duke of Kangle county.
translations.idiomatic: As regent, the court made him Palace Attendant and inspector of Jiangzhou with full command, and changed his title to Duke of Kangle.

sentences.zh: 及司徒陸法和據郢州，引齊兵來寇，乃使瑱西討，未至而法和入齊。

translations.literal: When the Minister of Works Lu Fazhi held Yingzhou and brought Qi troops to invade, Zhen was sent west to suppress him; before he arrived Fazhi had gone over to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of Works Lu Fazhi held Yingzhou and called in Qi troops, Zhen was sent west against him, but Fazhi submitted to Qi before he arrived.

sentences.zh: 齊遣慕容恃德鎮夏首，瑱攻之，恃德食盡請和，瑱還鎮豫章。

translations.literal: Qi sent Murong Shide to hold Xiashou; Zhen attacked him, and when Shide's provisions were exhausted he sued for peace; Zhen returned to garrison Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Qi posted Murong Shide at Xiashou; Zhen besieged him until he sued for peace, then returned to Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 僧辯使其弟僧愔與瑱共討蕭勃，及陳武帝誅僧辯，僧愔陰欲圖瑱而奪其軍，瑱知之，盡收僧愔徒黨，僧愔奔齊。

translations.literal: Senbian sent his younger brother Sengyin with Zhen to suppress Xiao Bo; when Chen the Emperor executed Senbian, Sengyin secretly plotted to destroy Zhen and seize his army. Zhen learned of it, arrested all of Sengyin's followers, and Sengyin fled to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Senbian sent his brother Sengyin with Zhen against Xiao Bo; after Chen Baxian killed Senbian, Sengyin plotted to seize Zhen's army. Zhen arrested his followers and Sengyin fled to Qi.

sentences.zh: 是時瑱據中流，甚強，又以本事王僧辯，雖外示臣節，未肯入朝。

translations.literal: At this time Hou Tian occupied the middle reaches of the river and was very strong; also, because he had originally served Wang Sengbian, although he outwardly displayed the etiquette of a subject, he was not willing to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Hou Tian occupied the middle reaches of the river and was very strong; also, because he had originally served Wang Sengbian, although he outwardly displayed the etiquette of a subject, he was not willing to enter court.

sentences.zh: 初，餘孝頃為豫章太守，及瑱鎮豫章，乃於新吳縣別立城柵，與瑱相拒。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yu Xiaoqing had been governor of Yuzhang; when Tian garrisoned Yuzhang, Xiaoqing separately established a fortified stockade in Xinwu County and opposed Tian.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yu Xiaoqing had been governor of Yuzhang; when Tian garrisoned Yuzhang, Xiaoqing separately established a fortified stockade in Xinwu County and opposed Tian.

sentences.zh: 瑱留軍人妻子於豫章，令從弟奫知後事，悉眾以攻孝頃，自夏迄冬弗能克。

translations.literal: Tian left the soldiers’ wives and children in Yuzhang, ordered his younger cousin Yun to manage the rear affairs, and attacked Xiaoqing with all his troops, but from summer through winter he could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Tian left the soldiers’ wives and children in Yuzhang, ordered his younger cousin Yun to manage the rear affairs, and attacked Xiaoqing with all his troops, but from summer through winter he could not overcome him.

sentences.zh: 奫與其部下侯方兒不協，方兒下攻奫，虜瑱軍府妓妾金玉，歸於武帝。

translations.literal: Yun did not get along with his subordinate Hou Fang’er; Fang’er went downriver and attacked Yun, seized the singing girls, concubines, gold, and jade from Tian’s military headquarters, and submitted them to Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Yun did not get along with his subordinate Hou Fang’er; Fang’er went downriver and attacked Yun, seized the singing girls, concubines, gold, and jade from Tian’s military headquarters, and submitted them to Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 瑱既失根本，輕歸豫章，豫章人拒之，乃趨盆城，就其將焦僧度。

translations.literal: After Tian lost his base, he hastily returned to Yuzhang, but the people of Yuzhang refused him, so he hurried to Pencheng and joined his commander Jiao Sengdu.
translations.idiomatic: After Tian lost his base, he hastily returned to Yuzhang, but the people of Yuzhang refused him, so he hurried to Pencheng and joined his commander Jiao Sengdu.

sentences.zh: 僧度勸瑱投齊，瑱以武帝有大量，必能容己，乃詣闕請罪，武帝復其爵位。

translations.literal: Sengdu urged Tian to defect to Qi, but Tian believed Emperor Wu was magnanimous and would surely tolerate him, so he went to the palace gate and requested punishment; Emperor Wu restored his noble rank and position.
translations.idiomatic: Sengdu urged Tian to defect to Qi, but Tian believed Emperor Wu was magnanimous and would surely tolerate him, so he went to the palace gate and requested punishment; Emperor Wu restored his noble rank and position.

sentences.zh: 永定二年，進位司空。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongding, Tian was advanced to the office of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongding, Tian was advanced to the office of Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 文帝即位，進授太尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Tian was advanced and appointed Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Tian was advanced and appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 王琳至柵口，又以瑱為都督，侯安都等並隸焉。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin reached Zhakou, Tian was again made commander-in-chief, with Hou Andu and the others all placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lin reached Zhakou, Tian was again made commander-in-chief, with Hou Andu and the others all placed under him.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年二月，王琳引合肥漅湖之眾，舳艫相次而下。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Tianjia, Wang Lin led the troops of Hefei and Chaohu, their warships following one another downstream.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Tianjia, Wang Lin led the troops of Hefei and Chaohu, their warships following one another downstream.

sentences.zh: 瑱率軍進獸檻洲。

translations.literal: Tian led the army forward to Shoujian Isle.
translations.idiomatic: Tian led the army forward to Shoujian Isle.

sentences.zh: 明日合戰，琳軍少卻。

translations.literal: The next day they joined battle, and Lin’s army drew back slightly.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they joined battle, and Lin’s army drew back slightly.

sentences.zh: 及夕，東北風吹其舟艦並壞。

translations.literal: By evening, a northeast wind blew and damaged all his boats and ships.
translations.idiomatic: By evening, a northeast wind blew and damaged all his boats and ships.

sentences.zh: 夜中有流星墜於賊營。

translations.literal: In the night a meteor fell into the rebel camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the night a meteor fell into the rebel camp.

sentences.zh: 及旦風靜，琳入浦，以鹿角繞岸，不敢復出。

translations.literal: At dawn the wind calmed; Lin entered an inlet and surrounded the bank with chevaux-de-frise, not daring to come out again.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the wind calmed; Lin entered an inlet and surrounded the bank with chevaux-de-frise, not daring to come out again.

sentences.zh: 時西魏將史寧躡其上流，瑱聞之，知琳不能持久，收軍卻據湖浦，以待其弊。

translations.literal: At the time the Western Wei general Shi Ning was pressing his upstream position; when Tian heard this, he knew Lin could not hold out for long, withdrew his army, occupied Hupu, and waited for Lin to become exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Western Wei general Shi Ning was pressing his upstream position; when Tian heard this, he knew Lin could not hold out for long, withdrew his army, occupied Hupu, and waited for Lin to become exhausted.

sentences.zh: 及史寧至，圍郢州，琳恐眾潰，乃率船東下，去蕪湖十里而泊。

translations.literal: When Shi Ning arrived and besieged Yingzhou, Lin feared his troops would collapse, so he led his ships eastward downstream and anchored ten li from Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Ning arrived and besieged Yingzhou, Lin feared his troops would collapse, so he led his ships eastward downstream and anchored ten li from Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 明日，齊人遣兵助琳，瑱令軍中晨炊蓐食，頓蕪湖洲尾以待之。

translations.literal: The next day, the Qi sent troops to aid Lin; Tian ordered the army to cook at dawn and eat early, and he stationed them at the tail of Wuhu Isle to await them.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, the Qi sent troops to aid Lin; Tian ordered the army to cook at dawn and eat early, and he stationed them at the tail of Wuhu Isle to await them.

sentences.zh: 將戰，有微風至自東南，眾軍施拍縱火，定州刺史章昭達乘平虜大艦中江而進，琳軍大敗，脫走以免者十二三，琳因此入齊。

translations.literal: As they were about to fight, a light wind came from the southeast; the armies set up battering devices and loosed fire, and Dingzhou Inspector Zhang Zhaoda rode a great Pacifying the Caitiffs warship forward in midstream. Lin’s army was badly defeated; only two or three out of ten escaped, and Lin accordingly entered Qi.
translations.idiomatic: As they were about to fight, a light wind came from the southeast; the armies set up battering devices and loosed fire, and Dingzhou Inspector Zhang Zhaoda rode a great Pacifying the Caitiffs warship forward in midstream. Lin’s army was badly defeated; only two or three out of ten escaped, and Lin accordingly entered Qi.

sentences.zh: 其年，詔以瑱為都督五州諸軍事，鎮盆城。

translations.literal: That year an edict made Zhen commander of military affairs in five provinces and stationed him at Pencheng.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was made commander of five provinces with his seat at Pencheng.

sentences.zh: 周將賀若敦、獨孤盛等來攻巴、湘，又以瑱為西討都督，大敗盛軍。

translations.literal: Zhou generals He Ruo Dun, Dugu Sheng, and others came to attack Ba and Xiang; Zhen was again made western campaign commander and routed Sheng's army utterly.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou generals He Ruo Dun and Dugu Sheng attacked Ba and Xiang, Zhen was made western commander and crushed Sheng's army.

sentences.zh: 以功授湘州刺史，改封零陵郡公。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed inspector of Xiangzhou and his fief was changed to Duke of Lingling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made inspector of Xiangzhou and Duke of Lingling.

sentences.zh: 二年薨，贈大司馬，諡曰壯肅，配享武帝廟庭。

translations.literal: In the second year he died; he was posthumously appointed Grand Marshal and given the posthumous title Stalwart and Solemn, with a place in the sacrifices at the Emperor's temple.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of his tenure and was posthumously made Grand Marshal with the posthumous name Zhuangsu, Stalwart and Solemn, and a place in Emperor Wu's temple.

sentences.zh: 子淨藏嗣，尚文帝女富陽公主。

translations.literal: His son Jingzang succeeded and married the Princess of Fuyang, daughter of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingzang succeeded him and married Emperor Wen's daughter, the Princess of Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 侯安都字成師，始興曲江人也，為郡著姓。

translations.literal: Hou Andou, courtesy name Chengshi, was a native of Qujiang in Shixing and came from a prominent family of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Andou, styled Chengshi, came from Qujiang in Shixing, a leading family of the region.

sentences.zh: 父捍，少仕州郡，以忠謹稱。

translations.literal: His father Han in youth served in the province and commandery and was known for loyalty and prudence.
translations.idiomatic: His father Han served in local office in youth and was known for loyalty and discretion.

sentences.zh: 安都貴後，官至光祿大夫、始興內史。

translations.literal: After Andou rose to eminence, Han reached the posts of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and interior minister of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: After Andou rose to power, his father reached the rank of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and interior minister of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 安都工隸書，能鼓琴，涉獵書傳，為五言詩頗清靡，兼善騎射，為邑裏雄豪。

translations.literal: Andou was skilled in clerical script, could play the zither, ranged widely in books and records, wrote five-character verse of refined elegance, and was also adept at riding and archery—a local champion.
translations.idiomatic: Andou wrote clerical script, played the zither, read widely, composed polished pentasyllabic verse, and excelled at riding and archery—the leading man of the district.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，招集兵甲，至三千人。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion he gathered arms and men, reaching three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled he raised three thousand armed men.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝入援臺城，安都引兵從武帝，攻蔡路養，破李遷仕，克平侯景，並力戰有功，封富川縣子。

translations.literal: When Chen the Emperor marched to relieve the capital, Andou led his troops to follow the Emperor, attacked Cai Luyang, defeated Li Qianshi, helped pacify Hou Jing, and in hard fighting won merit; he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Fuchuan county.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Baxian marched to relieve the capital, Andou followed him, fought Cai Luyang and Li Qianshi, helped destroy Hou Jing, and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Fuchuan.

sentences.zh: 隨武帝鎮京口，除蘭陵太守。

translations.literal: He followed the Emperor in garrisoning Jingkou and was appointed administrator of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Emperor to Jingkou and was made governor of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 武帝謀襲王僧辯，唯與安都定計。

translations.literal: When the Emperor plotted to strike Wang Senbian, he planned it only with Andou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor plotted against Wang Senbian, Andou alone shared the plan.

sentences.zh: 仍使安都率水軍自京口趣石頭，武帝自從江乘羅落會之。

translations.literal: He then had Andou lead the river force from Jingkou toward Shitou while he himself set out from Jiangcheng and Luoluo to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Andou led the fleet from Jingkou toward Shitou while the Emperor marched from Jiangcheng and Luoluo to meet him.

sentences.zh: 安都至石頭北，棄舟登岸，僧辯弗之覺。

translations.literal: Andou reached the north of Shitou, abandoned his boats, and went ashore—Senbian did not detect him.
translations.idiomatic: Andou reached the north bank of Shitou, landed his men, and Senbian never knew.

sentences.zh: 石頭城北接岡阜，不甚危峻，安都被甲，帶長刀，軍人捧之，投於女垣內，眾隨而入，進逼僧辯臥室。

translations.literal: The north of Shitou city adjoined hillocks and was not very steep; Andou donned armor, carried a long blade, and was lifted by his soldiers and thrown over the parapet; the host followed inside and pressed on to Senbian's bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: The north wall of Shitou was not steep; armored and sword in hand, Andou was hoisted over the parapet by his men, the troops poured in, and they reached Senbian's chamber.

sentences.zh: 武帝大軍亦至，與僧辯戰於聽事前，安都自內合出，腹背擊之，遂禽僧辯。

translations.literal: The Emperor's main army also arrived and fought Senbian before the audience hall; Andou sallied from within to join the attack from front and rear and captured Senbian alive.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's main force arrived and fought Senbian in the hall; Andou struck from within while the Emperor struck from without, and Senbian was taken alive.

sentences.zh: 以功授南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed inspector of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made inspector of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 武帝東討杜龕，安都留臺居守。

translations.literal: When the Emperor campaigned east against Du Kan, Andou remained to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor marched east against Du Kan, Andou stayed behind to defend the capital.

sentences.zh: 徐嗣徽、任約等引齊寇入據石頭，游騎至於闕下。

translations.literal: Xu Sihui, Ren Yue, and others brought Qi invaders in, seized Shitou, and their patrols reached the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Sihui and Ren Yue brought Qi troops in, seized Shitou, and their patrols rode to the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 安都閉門示弱，令城中登陴看賊者斬。

translations.literal: Andou shut the gates and feigned weakness, ordering that anyone in the city who mounted the walls to watch the enemy be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Andou shut the gates and played weak, executing anyone who climbed the walls to watch the enemy.

sentences.zh: 及夕，賊收軍還石頭。

translations.literal: By evening the enemy withdrew to Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk the enemy withdrew to Shitou.

sentences.zh: 安都夜令士卒密營禦敵之具。

translations.literal: At night Andou had his soldiers secretly prepare equipment for resisting the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: That night Andou had his men secretly prepare for battle.

sentences.zh: 將旦，賊騎至，安都與戰，大敗之，賊乃退還石頭，不敢逼臺城。

translations.literal: Near dawn the enemy cavalry arrived; Andou fought them and routed them utterly, and the enemy then withdrew to Shitou and did not dare press the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the enemy cavalry came; Andou routed them and they fled to Shitou, no longer daring to threaten the capital.

sentences.zh: 及武帝至，以安都為水軍。

translations.literal: When the Emperor arrived he put Andou in command of the river forces.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor arrived he put Andou in charge of the fleet.

sentences.zh: 于中流斷賊糧運。

translations.literal: On the river he cut the enemy's grain convoys.
translations.idiomatic: On the river he cut the enemy's supply lines.

sentences.zh: 又襲秦郡，破嗣徽柵，收其家口，得嗣徽所彈琵琶及所養鷹，遣信餉之，曰：「昨至弟住處，得此，今以相還。」

translations.literal: He also raided Qin Commandery, broke Sihui's stockade, took his family, obtained Sihui's pipa and hunting hawk, and sent them to him with a message, saying, "Yesterday I came to where your younger brother was staying and obtained these; now I return them to you."
translations.idiomatic: He also raided Qin Commandery, broke Sihui's stockade, took his family, obtained Sihui's pipa and hunting hawk, and sent them to him with a message, saying, "Yesterday I came to where your younger brother was staying and obtained these; now I return them to you."

sentences.zh: 嗣徽等見之大懼，尋求和，武帝聽其還北。

translations.literal: When Sihui and the others saw this they were greatly afraid and soon sued for peace; the Emperor allowed them to return north.
translations.idiomatic: Sihui was terrified and sued for peace; the Emperor let him withdraw north.

sentences.zh: 及嗣徽等濟江，齊之餘軍猶據採石，守備甚嚴，又遣安都攻之，多所俘獲。

translations.literal: After Sihui and the others crossed the river, Qi's remaining troops still held Caishi with very strict defenses; Andou was again sent to attack them and took many captives.
translations.idiomatic: After Sihui crossed the river, Qi troops still held Caishi; Andou attacked and took many prisoners.

sentences.zh: 明年春，詔安都率兵鎮梁山以備齊。

translations.literal: The next spring an edict ordered Andou to lead troops and garrison Liangshan against Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring he was ordered to garrison Liangshan against Qi.

sentences.zh: 徐嗣徽等復入，至湖熟，武帝追安都還拒之，戰于耕壇南。

translations.literal: Xu Sihui and the others invaded again as far as Hushu; the Emperor recalled Andou to resist them, and they fought south of Gengtan.
translations.idiomatic: Sihui invaded again as far as Hushu; the Emperor recalled Andou, and they fought south of Gengtan.

sentences.zh: 安都率十二騎突其陣，破之，禽齊儀同乞伏無芳，又刺齊將東方老墮馬，會賊騎至，救老，獲免。

translations.literal: Andou led twelve horsemen in a charge that broke the enemy line, captured the Qi honorary companion Qifu Wufang, and also speared the Qi general Dongfang Lao so that he fell from his horse; enemy cavalry then arrived and rescued Lao, who escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Andou charged with twelve horsemen, broke their line, captured Qifu Wufang, and speared Dongfang Lao from his horse before enemy riders rescued him.

sentences.zh: 賊北度蔣山。

translations.literal: The enemy fled north across Mount Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy fled north over Mount Jiang.

sentences.zh: 安都又與齊將王敬寶戰于龍尾，使從弟曉、軍主張纂前犯其陣，曉被創墜馬，張纂死之。

translations.literal: Andou again fought the Qi general Wang Jingbao at Longwei, sending his cousin Xiao and the commander Zhang Zuan to strike the enemy line first; Xiao was wounded and fell from his horse, and Zhang Zuan was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Andou fought Wang Jingbao at Longwei; his cousin Xiao and Zhang Zuan led the charge—Xiao was wounded and fell, and Zhang Zuan was killed.

sentences.zh: 安都馳往救曉，斬其騎士十二人，取纂屍而還，齊軍不敢逼。

translations.literal: Andou galloped to rescue Xiao, cut down twelve of the enemy horsemen, recovered Zhang Zuan's body and returned, and the Qi army did not dare press him.
translations.idiomatic: Andou rode to save Xiao, killed twelve enemy horsemen, recovered Zhang Zuan's body, and the Qi army dared not close on him.

sentences.zh: 武帝與齊軍戰于莫府山，命安都自白下橫擊其後，大敗之。

translations.literal: The Emperor fought the Qi army at Mofu Mountain and ordered Andou to strike their rear from Baixia in a flank attack, routing them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: At Mofu Mountain the Emperor ordered Andou to hit the Qi rear from Baixia, and they won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 以功進爵為侯，又進號平南將軍，改封西江縣公。

translations.literal: For his merit he was advanced to marquis, promoted to General Who Pacifies the South, and his fief was changed to Duke of Xijiang county.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made a marquis, promoted to General Who Pacifies the South, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xijiang.

sentences.zh: 仍督水軍出豫章，助豫州刺史周文育討蕭勃。

translations.literal: He again commanded the river forces out from Yuzhang to assist Zhou Wenyu, inspector of Yuzhou, in suppressing Xiao Bo.
translations.idiomatic: He led the fleet from Yuzhang to help Yuzhou inspector Zhou Wenyu against Xiao Bo.

sentences.zh: 安都未至，文育已斬勃，並禽其將歐陽頠、傅泰等。

translations.literal: Before Andou arrived, Wenyu had already beheaded Bo and captured his generals Ouyang Wei, Fu Tai, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Before Andou arrived, Wenyu had killed Bo and captured Ouyang Wei, Fu Tai, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 唯餘孝頃與勃子孜猶于豫章之石頭作兩城，孝頃與孜各據其一，又多設船艦，夾水而陣。
