translations.literal: Only Yu Xiaodun and Bo's son Zi still built two cities at Shitou in Yuzhang, each holding one, and they also deployed many ships in battle array on both sides of the water.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yu Xiaodun and Bo's son Zi still held twin forts at Shitou, one each, with fleets drawn up on both banks.

sentences.zh: 安都至，乃銜枚夜燒其艦。

translations.literal: When Andou arrived he had his men take gag-sticks in their mouths and at night burned their ships.
translations.idiomatic: Andou arrived and burned their fleet in a silent night attack.

sentences.zh: 文育率水軍，安都領步騎，登岸結陣。

translations.literal: Wenyu led the river force while Andou commanded infantry and cavalry; they went ashore and formed battle lines.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu led the fleet while Andou took the infantry and cavalry ashore in battle order.

sentences.zh: 孝頃俄斷後路，安都乃令軍士豎柵，引營漸進，頻致克獲，孜乃降。

translations.literal: Xiaodun soon cut off their retreat; Andou then ordered the soldiers to erect palisades and advance the camp step by step, winning repeated successes, and Zi then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaodun cut their retreat; Andou had palisades thrown up and advanced camp by camp until Zi surrendered.

sentences.zh: 孝頃奔歸新吳，請入子為質，許之。

translations.literal: Xiaodun fled back to Xinwu and asked to send his son as hostage; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaodun fled to Xinwu and offered his son as hostage; the offer was accepted.

sentences.zh: 以功加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: For his merit he was given the additional title Grand Master with the same privileges as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made Grand Master with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 仍率眾會武昌，與周文育西討王琳。

translations.literal: He again led his forces to assemble at Wuchang and join Zhou Wenyu in the western campaign against Wang Lin.
translations.idiomatic: He led his troops to Wuchang to join Zhou Wenyu's western campaign against Wang Lin.

sentences.zh: 將發，王公以下餞于新林，安都躍馬度橋，人馬俱墜水中。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, princes and officials below them gave a farewell at Xinlin; Andou spurred his horse across a bridge and both man and horse fell into the water.
translations.idiomatic: At the farewell at Xinlin, Andou spurred his horse over a bridge and horse and rider plunged into the water.

sentences.zh: 又坐鰨內墜于櫓井，時以為不祥。

translations.literal: He also sat in a covered boat and fell into the oar-well; at the time this was taken as an ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: He also fell into a ship's well from the cabin—omens of ill luck, people said.

sentences.zh: 至武昌，琳將樊猛棄城走，文育亦自豫章至。

translations.literal: When they reached Wuchang, Lin's general Fan Meng abandoned the city and fled; Wenyu also arrived from Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuchang, Wang Lin's general Fan Meng abandoned the city; Wenyu arrived from Yuzhang as well.

sentences.zh: 時兩將俱行，不相統攝，因部下交爭，稍不平。

translations.literal: At that time both generals marched together without unified command; because their subordinates quarreled, they were somewhat at odds.
translations.idiomatic: The two commanders advanced together but shared no chain of command, and quarrels among their men left them on uneasy terms.

sentences.zh: 軍至郢州，琳將潘純於城中遙射官軍，安都怒，圍之。

translations.literal: When the army reached Yingzhou, Wang Lin's general Pan Chun shot at the imperial army from the city at a distance; Andou was enraged and besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: At Yingzhou, Lin's general Pan Chun peppered the imperial forces from the walls; Andou flew into a rage and laid siege to the city.

sentences.zh: 未克，而王琳至弇口，安都乃釋郢州，悉眾往沌口以禦之，遇風不得進。

translations.literal: Before it was taken, Wang Lin reached Yankou; Andou then released Yingzhou, led his entire force to Dunkou to oppose him, and met wind and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Before the city fell, Wang Lin reached Yankou. Andou abandoned the siege, marched his whole army to Dunkou to block him, and was halted by contrary winds.

sentences.zh: 琳據東岸，官軍據西岸，相持數日，乃合戰。

translations.literal: Lin held the east bank and the imperial army the west bank; they faced each other for several days, then joined battle.
translations.idiomatic: Lin held the eastern shore, the imperial army the western; after several days of standoff they closed in battle.

sentences.zh: 安都等敗，與周文育、徐敬成並為琳囚，總以一長鎖系之，置於鰨下，令所親宦者王子晉掌視之。

translations.literal: Andou and the others were defeated; he, Zhou Wenyu, and Xu Jingcheng were all taken prisoner by Lin, bound together with one long chain, placed beneath the barracuda-boat, and entrusted to his favorite eunuch Wang Zijin to guard.
translations.idiomatic: Andou's force was beaten; he, Zhou Wenyu, and Xu Jingcheng were all Lin's prisoners, shackled on one long chain and stowed under the barracuda-boat while the eunuch Wang Zijin, whom Lin trusted, watched them.

sentences.zh: 琳下至盆城白水浦，安都等甘言許賂子晉，子晉乃偽以小船依鰨而釣，夜載安都、文育、敬成上岸，入深草，步投官軍。

translations.literal: When Lin went down to Baishui Ford at Pencheng, Andou and the others spoke sweet words and promised bribes to Zijin; Zijin then pretended to fish in a small boat alongside the barracuda-boat, and by night ferried Andou, Wenyu, and Jingcheng ashore; they entered deep grass and on foot reached the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: At Pencheng's Baishui Ford, Andou and his companions flattered Zijin and promised him reward; Zijin feigned angling from a skiff beside the barracuda-boat and under cover of night rowed Andou, Wenyu, and Jingcheng ashore. They stole through tall grass and on foot rejoined the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 還都自劾，詔並赦之，復其官爵。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital they impeached themselves; an edict pardoned them all and restored their offices and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital they submitted self-accusations; the throne pardoned them and restored rank and office.

sentences.zh: 尋為丹陽尹，出為南豫州刺史，令繼周文育攻餘孝勱及王琳將曹慶、常眾愛等。

translations.literal: Soon he became Governor of Danyang, then went out as Inspector of South Yuzhou, ordered to succeed Zhou Wenyu in attacking Yu Xiaoxun and Wang Lin's generals Cao Qing, Chang Zhong'ai, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made governor of Danyang, then sent out as inspector of South Yuzhou to carry on Zhou Wenyu's campaign against Yu Xiaoxun and Wang Lin's generals Cao Qing and Chang Zhong'ai.

sentences.zh: 安都自宮亭湖出松門，躡眾愛後。

translations.literal: Andou left Gongting Lake by Songmen and pressed on Zhong'ai's rear.
translations.idiomatic: Andou issued from Gongting Lake through Songmen and harried Zhong'ai's retreat.

sentences.zh: 文育為熊曇朗所害，安都回取大艦，遇琳將周炅、周協南歸，與戰，破之，禽炅、協。

translations.literal: Wenyu was killed by Xiong Tanlang; Andou turned back to seize large warships, met Wang Lin's generals Zhou Jiong and Zhou Xie returning south, fought them, defeated them, and captured Jiong and Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu fell to Xiong Tanlang; Andou doubled back for the great ships, intercepted Lin's generals Zhou Jiong and Zhou Xie marching south, routed them, and took both captive.

sentences.zh: 孝勱弟孝猷率部下四千家，欲就王琳，遇炅敗，乃詣安都降。

translations.literal: Xiaoxun's younger brother Xiaoyou led four thousand families of his following, intending to join Wang Lin; meeting Jiong's defeat, he thereupon came to Andou and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxun's brother Xiaoyou led four thousand households toward Wang Lin; after Jiong's rout he submitted to Andou instead.

sentences.zh: 安都又進軍於禽奇洲，破曹慶、常眾愛等，焚其船艦。

translations.literal: Andou again advanced to Qinqi Isle, defeated Cao Qing, Chang Zhong'ai, and the rest, and burned their ships.
translations.idiomatic: Andou pushed on to Qinqi Isle, broke Cao Qing and Chang Zhong'ai, and burned their fleet.

sentences.zh: 眾愛奔廬山，為村人所殺，余眾悉平。

translations.literal: Zhong'ai fled to Mount Lu and was killed by villagers; the remaining forces were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong'ai fled to Mount Lu, where villagers killed him; the rest of the enemy were brought to order.

sentences.zh: 還軍至南皖，而武帝崩，安都隨文帝還朝，乃與群臣議，翼奉文帝。

translations.literal: Returning, the army reached Nanwan when the Emperor died; Andou followed Emperor Wen back to court and deliberated with the ministers, hoping to install Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: The army was at Nanwan when Chen Baxian died; Andou returned to court with Emperor Wen and joined the ministers in pressing Wen's enthronement.

sentences.zh: 時帝謙讓弗敢當，太后又以衡陽王故，未肯下令，群臣不能決。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor modestly declined and dared not accept; the empress dowager, because of the Prince of Hengyang, also would not issue the order; the ministers could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Wen demurred; the empress dowager, mindful of the Prince of Hengyang, would not issue the decree; the court could reach no decision.

sentences.zh: 安都曰：「今四方未定，何暇及遠。

translations.literal: Andou said: "The four quarters are not yet settled—what leisure is there to look afar?
translations.idiomatic: Andou said, "The realm is still unsettled—who has time for distant claims?

sentences.zh: 臨川王有功天下，須共立之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Linchuan has merit under Heaven; he must be enthroned together.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Linchuan has served the realm; we must raise him together.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，後應者斬。」

translations.literal: Whoever responds later in today's affair will be beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever responds later in today's affair will be beheaded."

sentences.zh: 便按劍上殿，白太后出璽，又手解文帝發，推就喪次。

translations.literal: He then drew his sword, went up the hall, told the empress dowager to produce the seal, and with his own hands unbound Emperor Wen's hair and pushed him to the mourning place.
translations.idiomatic: He drew his sword, strode into the hall, demanded the seal from the empress dowager, loosed Wen's hair with his own hands, and thrust him to the mourning seat.

sentences.zh: 文帝即位，遷司空，仍授南徐州刺史，給扶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Andou was transferred to Minister of Works and was also appointed Inspector of South Xuzhou, with an allowance of staff.
translations.idiomatic: On Wen's accession, Andou became minister of works and inspector of South Xuzhou, with the staff befitting his rank.

sentences.zh: 王琳下至柵口，大軍出頓蕪湖。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin came down to Zhakou, the main army went out and encamped at Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: As Wang Lin descended on Zhakou, the main force encamped at Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 時侯瑱為大都督，而指麾經略多出安都。

translations.literal: At the time Hou Zhen was grand commander, but direction and strategy mostly came from Andou.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Zhen held the grand command, yet planning and orders largely issued from Andou.

sentences.zh: 及王琳入齊，安都進軍盆城，討琳餘党，所向皆下。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin entered Qi, Andou advanced on Pencheng to suppress Lin's remaining partisans; wherever he went, all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: After Lin fled to Qi, Andou marched on Pencheng against his remnants and swept all before him.

sentences.zh: 仍別奉中旨，迎衡陽獻王昌。

translations.literal: He also separately received a secret order to welcome the Offered Prince of Hengyang, Wang Chang.
translations.idiomatic: He also received a secret charge to welcome the Offered Prince of Hengyang, Wang Chang.

sentences.zh: 初昌之將入，致書于文帝，辭甚不遜。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chang was about to enter, he sent a letter to Emperor Wen, its wording very insubordinate.
translations.idiomatic: Before Chang's arrival he had written to Emperor Wen in grossly insubordinate terms.

sentences.zh: 帝不懌，召安都，從容而言曰：「太子將至，須別求一蕃，吾其老焉。」

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased, summoned Andou, and said calmly, "The heir apparent will soon arrive; I must separately seek a frontier domain and grow old there."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased, summoned Andou, and said calmly, "The heir apparent will soon arrive; I must separately seek a frontier domain and grow old there."

sentences.zh: 安都對曰：「自古豈有被代天子，愚臣不敢奉詔。」

translations.literal: Andou replied: "Since antiquity has there ever been a Son of Heaven who was replaced? This foolish subject dares not receive such an order.
translations.idiomatic: Andou answered, "When has a Son of Heaven ever been replaced? Your servant dares not obey."

sentences.zh: 因自迎昌，中流而殺之。

translations.literal: He thereupon went himself to welcome Chang and killed him midstream.
translations.idiomatic: He went in person to meet Chang and killed him on the river.

sentences.zh: 以功進爵清遠郡公。

translations.literal: For his merit he was advanced in rank to Duke of Qingyuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was made duke of Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 自是威名甚重，群臣無出其右。

translations.literal: From this his martial renown weighed very heavily, and among the ministers none surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: His prestige now outweighed every minister at court.

sentences.zh: 安都父捍為始興內史，卒于官，文帝征安都為發喪。

translations.literal: Andou's father Han served as interior governor of Shixing and died in office; Emperor Wen summoned Andou to conduct the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Andou's father Han had been interior governor of Shixing and died in post; Wen recalled Andou to bury him.

sentences.zh: 尋起復本官，贈其父散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫，拜其母為清遠國太夫人，仍迎赴都。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled to his former office; his father was posthumously made Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; his mother was appointed Lady of Qingyuan state, and she was welcomed to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resumed office; his father was posthumously honored, his mother made Lady of Qingyuan and brought to the capital.

sentences.zh: 母固求停鄉里，上乃下詔，改桂陽郡之汝城縣為盧陽郡，分衡州之始興、安遠二郡，合三郡為東衡州，以安都從弟曉為刺史。

translations.literal: His mother firmly asked to remain in her native district; the sovereign then issued an edict changing Rucheng county in Guiyang commandery to Luyang commandery, dividing the two commanderies of Shixing and Anyuan in Hengzhou and combining three commanderies into East Hengzhou, with Andou's younger cousin Xiao as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: She begged to stay home; the throne created Luyang commandery from Rucheng, formed East Hengzhou from three districts, and made Andou's cousin Xiao its inspector.

sentences.zh: 安都第三子秘年九歲，上以為始興內史，並令在鄉侍養。

translations.literal: Andou's third son Mi was nine years old; the sovereign made him interior governor of Shixing and ordered him to remain in the district to attend his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Andou's third son Mi, nine years old, was named interior governor of Shixing and left in the country to care for her.

sentences.zh: 改封安都桂陽郡公。

translations.literal: Andou's enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Guiyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Andou was re-enfeoffed as duke of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 王琳敗後，周兵入據巴、湘，安都奉詔西捍。

translations.literal: After Wang Lin's defeat, Zhou troops entered and held Ba and Xiang; Andou received orders to defend the west.
translations.idiomatic: After Lin's fall, Northern Zhou held Ba and Xiang; Andou was ordered west to hold them.

sentences.zh: 及留異擁據東陽，又奉詔東討。

translations.literal: When Liu Yi seized and held Dongyang, he again received orders to campaign east.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yi seized Dongyang, he was sent east again.

sentences.zh: 異本謂台軍自錢唐江上，安都乃步由會稽之諸暨，出永康。

translations.literal: Yi had expected the imperial army to come up the Qiantang River; Andou instead marched overland through Zhuji in Kuaiji and out by Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: Yi expected the court army up the Qiantang; Andou marched overland through Zhuji in Kuaiji and emerged at Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 異大恐，奔桃枝嶺，處岩穀間，豎柵以拒守。

translations.literal: Yi was greatly afraid, fled to Taozhi Ridge, took position in ravines and valleys, and erected palisades to resist and hold.
translations.idiomatic: In panic Yi fled to Taozhi Ridge, entrenched in the gorges, and threw up palisades.

sentences.zh: 安都躬自接戰，為流矢所中，血流至踝。

translations.literal: Andou personally joined the fighting, was struck by a stray arrow, and blood flowed to his ankles.
translations.idiomatic: Andou fought in the front rank, took a stray arrow, and blood ran to his ankles.

sentences.zh: 安都乘輿麾軍，容止不變。

translations.literal: Andou rode in his carriage to command the army; his bearing did not change.
translations.idiomatic: He still rode his carriage to direct the battle, his composure unbroken.

sentences.zh: 因其山隴為堰。

translations.literal: He used the mountain ridges to build a dam.
translations.idiomatic: He dammed the mountain streams.

sentences.zh: 屬夏潦水漲，安都引船入堰，樓艦與異城等，放拍碎其樓雉。

translations.literal: In summer the flood waters rose; Andou led ships into the dam, his tower ships level with Yi's walls, and loosed rams that smashed the parapets.
translations.idiomatic: Summer floods rose; he brought warships into the reservoir until his towers stood level with Yi's walls and sent rams that shattered the parapets.

sentences.zh: 異與第二子忠臣脫身奔晉安，虜其妻子，振旅而歸。

translations.literal: Yi and his second son Zhongchen escaped to Jin'an; Andou captured his wife and children and returned in martial array.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and his son Zhongchen fled to Jin'an; Andou took their families and marched home in triumph.

sentences.zh: 加侍中、征北大將軍，仍還本鎮。

translations.literal: He was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Campaigns North, and returned to his original command.
translations.idiomatic: He was made attendant-in-ordinary and general who campaigns north, then returned to his old post.

sentences.zh: 吏人詣闕，表請立碑頌美安都功績，詔許之。

translations.literal: Officials and people went to the court, memorializing to erect a stele praising Andou's achievements; the edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Local officers petitioned for a stele in his honor; the throne assented.

sentences.zh: 自王琳平後，安都勳庸轉大，又自以功安社稷，漸驕矜。

translations.literal: After Wang Lin was pacified, Andou's merit and service grew ever greater; he also considered that his achievement had settled the altars of state, and gradually became arrogant and proud.
translations.idiomatic: After Lin's fall Andou's laurels and self-regard swelled; he believed he had secured the dynasty and grew arrogant.

sentences.zh: 招聚文武士，騎馭馳騁，或命以詩筆，第其高下，以差次賞賜之。

translations.literal: He gathered civil and military men, rode and galloped, sometimes ordered them to compose verse or prose, ranked their quality high or low, and rewarded them in graded order.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered scholars and warriors, raced horses, set them to verse or prose, ranked their work, and paid them accordingly.

sentences.zh: 文士則褚玠、馬樞、陰鏗、張正見、徐伯陽、劉刪、祖孫登，武士則蕭摩訶、裴子烈等，並為之賓，齋內動至千人。

translations.literal: Among literary men were Chu Ci, Ma Shu, Yin Keng, Zhang Zhengjian, Xu Boyang, Liu Shan, and Zu Sundeng; among martial men were Xiao Mohe and Pei Zilie and others—all became his guests, and within his residence there were often as many as a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Writers such as Chu Ci, Ma Shu, Yin Keng, Zhang Zhengjian, Xu Boyang, Liu Shan, and Zu Sundeng, and fighters such as Xiao Mohe and Pei Zilie, flocked to his hall—often a thousand at once.

sentences.zh: 部下將帥，多不遵法度，檢問收攝，則奔歸安都。

translations.literal: The generals under his command mostly did not observe the law; when investigated and seized, they fled back to Andou.
translations.idiomatic: His officers routinely broke the law; whenever the court moved against them, they fled to Andou's protection.

sentences.zh: 文帝性嚴察，深銜之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen was by nature strict and observant and deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen, strict and watchful by nature, deeply resented it.

sentences.zh: 安都日益驕慢，表啟封訖，有事未盡，乃開封自書之，雲又啟某事。

translations.literal: Andou grew daily more arrogant; after sealing a memorial, if something remained unsaid, he would open the seal and write in it himself, saying he also memorialized on such-and-such a matter.
translations.idiomatic: He grew bolder still: having sealed a memorial, he would break it open to add lines—"I also report such-and-such."

sentences.zh: 及侍宴酒酣，或箕踞傾倚。

translations.literal: When attending banquets and wine was deep, he would sometimes sit with legs sprawled or lean askew.
translations.idiomatic: At court feasts, drunk, he sprawled or slouched against the furnishings.

sentences.zh: 嘗陪樂遊禊飲，乃白帝曰：「何如作臨川王時？」

translations.literal: Once, when accompanying the emperor at a purification feast at Leyou, he said to the emperor, "How does this compare with when you were Prince of Linchuan?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, when accompanying the emperor at a purification feast at Leyou, he said to the emperor, "How does this compare with when you were Prince of Linchuan?"

sentences.zh: 帝不應。

translations.literal: The emperor did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not reply.

sentences.zh: 安都再三言之，帝曰：「此雖天命，抑亦明公之力。」

translations.literal: Andou said this again and again, and the emperor replied, "Although this was Heaven's mandate, it was also your lordship's strength."
translations.idiomatic: Andou said this again and again, and the emperor replied, "Although this was Heaven's mandate, it was also your lordship's strength."

sentences.zh: 宴訖，又啟便借供張水飾，將載妻妾于禦堂歡會，帝雖許其請，甚不懌。

translations.literal: When the banquet ended, he again memorialized asking to borrow furnishings and aquatic decorations, intending to bring his wives and concubines to revel in the Imperial Hall; though the emperor granted the request, he was very displeased.
translations.idiomatic: After the feast he asked to borrow palace furnishings and aquatic décor to bring his wives and concubines for a revel in the Imperial Hall; Wen consented but was furious.

sentences.zh: 明日，安都坐於御坐，賓客居群臣位，稱觴上壽。

translations.literal: The next day Andou sat on the imperial seat; his guests occupied the ministers' places and raised cups to wish long life.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Andou took the throne; his guests sat where the ministers should have been and offered toasts.

sentences.zh: 初，重雲殿災，安都率將士帶甲入殿，帝甚惡之，自是陰為之備。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chongyun Hall burned, Andou had led armored soldiers into the hall; the emperor greatly detested this and from then secretly made preparations against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongyun Hall had burned, Andou had marched armed men inside; the emperor never forgave it and quietly prepared against him.

sentences.zh: 又周迪之反，朝望當使安都討之。

translations.literal: Again, when Zhou Di rebelled, the court expected that Andou would be sent to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Di rebelled, the court had expected Andou to crush him.

sentences.zh: 帝乃使吳明徹討迪。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore sent Wu Mingche to campaign against Di.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore sent Wu Mingche to campaign against Di.

sentences.zh: 又頻遣臺使案問安都部下，檢括亡叛，安都內不自安。

translations.literal: He also repeatedly sent court envoys to investigate Andu’s subordinates and search out fugitives and rebels, and Andu felt inwardly uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: He also repeatedly sent court envoys to investigate Andu’s subordinates and search out fugitives and rebels, and Andu felt inwardly uneasy.

sentences.zh: 天嘉三年冬，遣其別駕周玄實自託於舍人蔡景歷，并問省中事，景歷錄其狀，奏之稱安都謀反，帝慮其不受召。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Tianjia, Andu sent his aide Zhou Xuanshi to entrust himself to Palace Aide Cai Jingli and also ask about affairs inside the palace; Jingli recorded the circumstances and memorialized that Andu was plotting rebellion, and the emperor feared that Andu would not accept a summons.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year of Tianjia, Andu sent his aide Zhou Xuanshi to entrust himself to Palace Aide Cai Jingli and also ask about affairs inside the palace; Jingli recorded the circumstances and memorialized that Andu was plotting rebellion, and the emperor feared that Andu would not accept a summons.

sentences.zh: 明年春，乃除安都為征南大將軍、江州刺史，自京口還都，部伍入於石頭，帝引安都宴於嘉德殿，又集其部下將帥會於尚書朝堂，於坐收安都，囚於西省。

translations.literal: In the spring of the following year, the emperor therefore appointed Andu Grand General Who Campaigns South and inspector of Jiangzhou. Andu returned from Jingkou to the capital, and when his units entered Shitou, the emperor drew Andu in for a banquet in Jiade Hall and also assembled his subordinate commanders for a gathering at the court hall of the Secretariat; during the sitting he arrested Andu and imprisoned him in the western office.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the following year, the emperor therefore appointed Andu Grand General Who Campaigns South and inspector of Jiangzhou. Andu returned from Jingkou to the capital, and when his units entered Shitou, the emperor drew Andu in for a banquet in Jiade Hall and also assembled his subordinate commanders for a gathering at the court hall of the Secretariat; during the sitting he arrested Andu and imprisoned him in the western office.

sentences.zh: 又收其將帥，盡奪馬仗而釋之，因出景歷表於朝，乃下詔暴其罪。

translations.literal: He also arrested Andu’s commanders, stripped them all of their horses and weapons, and released them; then he brought Jingli’s memorial out before the court and issued an edict exposing Andu’s crimes.
translations.idiomatic: He also arrested Andu’s commanders, stripped them all of their horses and weapons, and released them; then he brought Jingli’s memorial out before the court and issued an edict exposing Andu’s crimes.

sentences.zh: 明日於西省賜死。

translations.literal: The next day, Andu was granted death in the western office.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, Andu was granted death in the western office.

sentences.zh: 尋有詔宥其妻子家口，葬以士禮。

translations.literal: Soon an edict pardoned his wife, children, and household and buried him with the rites of a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict pardoned his wife, children, and household and buried him with the rites of a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 安都第三子秘年九歲，上以為始興內史，並令在鄉侍養。

translations.literal: Andu’s third son Mi was nine years old; the emperor made him administrator of Shixing and ordered him to remain in his home district to serve and support his elders.
translations.idiomatic: Andu’s third son Mi was nine years old; the emperor made him administrator of Shixing and ordered him to remain in his home district to serve and support his elders.

sentences.zh: 初，武帝嘗與諸將宴杜僧明、周文育、侯安都為壽，各稱功伐。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Wu once banqueted with the generals, while Du Sengming, Zhou Wenyu, and Hou Andu offered birthday toasts, each speaking of his campaigns and achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Wu once banqueted with the generals, while Du Sengming, Zhou Wenyu, and Hou Andu offered birthday toasts, each speaking of his campaigns and achievements.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿等悉良將也，而並有所短。

translations.literal: The emperor said, “You gentlemen are all good generals, but each of you has shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, “You gentlemen are all good generals, but each of you has shortcomings.

sentences.zh: 杜公志大而識暗，狎於下而驕於尊，矜其功，不收其拙。

translations.literal: Lord Du has great ambition but dim judgment; he is familiar with those below and arrogant toward those above, boasts of his achievements, and does not restrain his clumsiness.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Du has great ambition but dim judgment; he is familiar with those below and arrogant toward those above, boasts of his achievements, and does not restrain his clumsiness.

sentences.zh: 周侯交不擇人，而推心過差，居危履險，猜防不設。

translations.literal: Marquis Zhou does not choose carefully in friendship and is excessive in laying bare his heart; dwelling in danger and treading peril, he sets no guard of suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Zhou does not choose carefully in friendship and is excessive in laying bare his heart; dwelling in danger and treading peril, he sets no guard of suspicion.

sentences.zh: 侯郎傲誕而無厭，輕佻而肆志，並非全身之道。」

translations.literal: Young Hou is arrogant, reckless, and insatiable, frivolous and unrestrained in his desires; none of these are ways to preserve one’s body whole.”
translations.idiomatic: Young Hou is arrogant, reckless, and insatiable, frivolous and unrestrained in his desires; none of these are ways to preserve one’s body whole.”

sentences.zh: 卒皆如言。

translations.literal: In the end, all happened as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, all happened as he had said.

sentences.zh: 太建三年，宣帝追封安都陳集縣侯。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taijian, Emperor Xuan posthumously enfeoffed Andu as Marquis of Chenji County.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taijian, Emperor Xuan posthumously enfeoffed Andu as Marquis of Chenji County.

sentences.zh: 子亶為嗣。

translations.literal: His son Dan succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 歐陽頠字靖世，長沙臨湘人也。

translations.literal: Ouyang Wei, styled Jingshi, was from Linxiang in Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Wei, styled Jingshi, was from Linxiang in Changsha.

sentences.zh: 為郡豪族，少質直有思理，以言行著於嶺表。

translations.literal: His family was a powerful clan in the commandery; when young he was simple, upright, and thoughtful, and he was known beyond the passes for his words and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His family was a powerful clan in the commandery; when young he was simple, upright, and thoughtful, and he was known beyond the passes for his words and conduct.

sentences.zh: 父喪，哀毀甚，至家產累積悉讓諸兄，廬於麓山寺傍，專精習業，博通經史。

translations.literal: At his father’s mourning, his grief and self-wasting were extreme; he even yielded all the accumulated family property to his elder brothers, lived in a hut beside Lushan Monastery, devoted himself single-mindedly to study, and became widely versed in the Classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: At his father’s mourning, his grief and self-wasting were extreme; he even yielded all the accumulated family property to his elder brothers, lived in a hut beside Lushan Monastery, devoted himself single-mindedly to study, and became widely versed in the Classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 年三十，其兄逼令從官。

translations.literal: At the age of thirty, his elder brothers forced him to take office.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of thirty, his elder brothers forced him to take office.

sentences.zh: 梁左衛將軍蘭欽少與頠善，故頠常隨欽征討。

translations.literal: Lan Qin, General of the Left Guard under Liang, had been friendly with Wei when young, and for that reason Wei often followed Qin on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Qin, General of the Left Guard under Liang, had been friendly with Wei when young, and for that reason Wei often followed Qin on campaigns.

sentences.zh: 改封安都桂陽郡公。

translations.literal: Andou's enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Guiyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Andou was re-enfeoffed as duke of Guiyang.

translations.literal: After Wang Lin's defeat, Zhou troops entered and held Ba and Xiang; Andou received orders to defend the west.
translations.idiomatic: After Lin's fall, Northern Zhou held Ba and Xiang; Andou was ordered west to hold them.

translations.idiomatic: He still rode his carriage to direct the battle, his composure unbroken.

sentences.zh: 因其山隴為堰。

translations.literal: He used the mountain ridges to build a dam.
translations.idiomatic: He dammed the mountain streams.

sentences.zh: 屬夏潦水漲，安都引船入堰，樓艦與異城等，放拍碎其樓雉。

translations.literal: In summer the flood waters rose; Andou led ships into the dam, his tower ships level with Yi's walls, and loosed rams that smashed the parapets.
translations.idiomatic: Summer floods rose; he brought warships into the reservoir until his towers stood level with Yi's walls and sent rams that shattered the parapets.

sentences.zh: 異與第二子忠臣脫身奔晉安，虜其妻子，振旅而歸。

translations.literal: Yi and his second son Zhongchen escaped to Jin'an; Andou captured his wife and children and returned in martial array.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and his son Zhongchen fled to Jin'an; Andou took their families and marched home in triumph.

sentences.zh: 加侍中、征北大將軍，仍還本鎮。

translations.literal: He was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Campaigns North, and returned to his original command.
translations.idiomatic: He was made attendant-in-ordinary and general who campaigns north, then returned to his old post.

sentences.zh: 吏人詣闕，表請立碑頌美安都功績，詔許之。

translations.literal: Officials and people went to the court, memorializing to erect a stele praising Andou's achievements; the edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Local officers petitioned for a stele in his honor; the throne assented.

sentences.zh: 自王琳平後，安都勳庸轉大，又自以功安社稷，漸驕矜。

translations.literal: After Wang Lin was pacified, Andou's merit and service grew ever greater; he also considered that his achievement had settled the altars of state, and gradually became arrogant and proud.
translations.idiomatic: After Lin's fall Andou's laurels and self-regard swelled; he believed he had secured the dynasty and grew arrogant.

sentences.zh: 招聚文武士，騎馭馳騁，或命以詩筆，第其高下，以差次賞賜之。

translations.literal: He gathered civil and military men, rode and galloped, sometimes ordered them to compose verse or prose, ranked their quality high or low, and rewarded them in graded order.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered scholars and warriors, raced horses, set them to verse or prose, ranked their work, and paid them accordingly.

sentences.zh: 文士則褚玠、馬樞、陰鏗、張正見、徐伯陽、劉刪、祖孫登，武士則蕭摩訶、裴子烈等，並為之賓，齋內動至千人。

translations.literal: Among literary men were Chu Ci, Ma Shu, Yin Keng, Zhang Zhengjian, Xu Boyang, Liu Shan, and Zu Sundeng; among martial men were Xiao Mohe and Pei Zilie and others—all became his guests, and within his residence there were often as many as a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Writers such as Chu Ci, Ma Shu, Yin Keng, Zhang Zhengjian, Xu Boyang, Liu Shan, and Zu Sundeng, and fighters such as Xiao Mohe and Pei Zilie, flocked to his hall—often a thousand at once.

sentences.zh: 部下將帥，多不遵法度，檢問收攝，則奔歸安都。

translations.literal: The generals under his command mostly did not observe the law; when investigated and seized, they fled back to Andou.
translations.idiomatic: His officers routinely broke the law; whenever the court moved against them, they fled to Andou's protection.

sentences.zh: 文帝性嚴察，深銜之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen was by nature strict and observant and deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen, strict and watchful by nature, deeply resented it.

sentences.zh: 安都日益驕慢，表啟封訖，有事未盡，乃開封自書之，雲又啟某事。

translations.literal: Andou grew daily more arrogant; after sealing a memorial, if something remained unsaid, he would open the seal and write in it himself, saying he also memorialized on such-and-such a matter.
translations.idiomatic: He grew bolder still: having sealed a memorial, he would break it open to add lines—"I also report such-and-such."

sentences.zh: 及侍宴酒酣，或箕踞傾倚。

translations.literal: When attending banquets and wine was deep, he would sometimes sit with legs sprawled or lean askew.
translations.idiomatic: At court feasts, drunk, he sprawled or slouched against the furnishings.

sentences.zh: 嘗陪樂遊禊飲，乃白帝曰：「何如作臨川王時？」

translations.literal: Once, when accompanying the emperor at a purification feast at Leyou, he said to the emperor, "How does this compare with when you were Prince of Linchuan?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, when accompanying the emperor at a purification feast at Leyou, he said to the emperor, "How does this compare with when you were Prince of Linchuan?"

sentences.zh: 帝不應。

translations.literal: The emperor did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not reply.

sentences.zh: 安都再三言之，帝曰：「此雖天命，抑亦明公之力。」

translations.literal: Andou said this again and again, and the emperor replied, "Although this was Heaven's mandate, it was also your lordship's strength."
translations.idiomatic: Andou said this again and again, and the emperor replied, "Although this was Heaven's mandate, it was also your lordship's strength."

sentences.zh: 宴訖，又啟便借供張水飾，將載妻妾于禦堂歡會，帝雖許其請，甚不懌。

translations.literal: When the banquet ended, he again memorialized asking to borrow furnishings and aquatic decorations, intending to bring his wives and concubines to revel in the Imperial Hall; though the emperor granted the request, he was very displeased.
translations.idiomatic: After the feast he asked to borrow palace furnishings and aquatic décor to bring his wives and concubines for a revel in the Imperial Hall; Wen consented but was furious.

sentences.zh: 明日，安都坐於御坐，賓客居群臣位，稱觴上壽。

translations.literal: The next day Andou sat on the imperial seat; his guests occupied the ministers' places and raised cups to wish long life.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Andou took the throne; his guests sat where the ministers should have been and offered toasts.

sentences.zh: 初，重雲殿災，安都率將士帶甲入殿，帝甚惡之，自是陰為之備。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chongyun Hall burned, Andou had led armored soldiers into the hall; the emperor greatly detested this and from then secretly made preparations against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongyun Hall had burned, Andou had marched armed men inside; the emperor never forgave it and quietly prepared against him.

sentences.zh: 欽南征夷獠，禽陳文徹，所獲不可勝計，獻大銅鼓，累代所無。

translations.literal: When Qin campaigned south against the Yi and Lao, he captured Chen Wenche, took spoils beyond counting, and presented a great bronze drum, something unmatched for generations.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin campaigned south against the Yi and Lao, he captured Chen Wenche, took spoils beyond counting, and presented a great bronze drum, something unmatched for generations.

sentences.zh: 頠預其功，還為直合將軍。

translations.literal: Wei shared in the achievement and on returning became a direct-palace general.
translations.idiomatic: Wei shared the credit and, on return, was made a direct-palace general.

sentences.zh: 欽征交州，復啟頠同行。

translations.literal: When Qin campaigned on Jiaozhou, he again requested that Wei accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lan Qin marched on Jiaozhou, he again asked Wei to go with him.

sentences.zh: 欽度嶺而卒，頠除臨賀內史，啟乞送欽喪還都，然後之任。

translations.literal: Qin crossed the ranges and died; Wei was appointed interior governor of Linhe, memorialized asking to escort Qin's coffin back to the capital, and only then took up his post.
translations.idiomatic: Qin died crossing the mountains; Wei was named governor of Linhe, begged leave to send Qin's body home, then took office.

sentences.zh: 時湘、衡界五十餘洞不賓，敕衡州刺史韋粲討之。

translations.literal: At the time more than fifty cave settlements on the border of Xiang and Heng were unsubmissive; an edict ordered Wei Can, inspector of Hengzhou, to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: More than fifty hill settlements along the Xiang–Heng frontier were in revolt; the throne ordered Hengzhou inspector Wei Can to subdue them.

sentences.zh: 粲委頠為都督，悉皆平殄。

translations.literal: Can entrusted Wei as commander-in-chief; all were pacified and exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Can put Wei in command; every stronghold was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 侯景構逆，粲自解還都征景，以頠監衡州。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing raised rebellion, Can resigned his post and returned to the capital to campaign against Jing, making Wei overseer of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, Can resigned to march on the capital and left Wei to oversee Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 臺城陷後，嶺南互相吞併，蘭欽弟前高州刺史裕攻始興內史蕭昭基，奪其郡。

translations.literal: After the capital fell, Lingnan swallowed one another; Lan Qin's younger brother, former inspector of Gaozhou Yu, attacked the interior governor of Shixing Xiao Zhaoji and seized his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital fell, the south devoured itself; Lan Qin's brother Yu, former Gaozhou inspector, attacked Shixing governor Xiao Zhaoji and seized his district.

sentences.zh: 以兄欽與頠舊，遣招之。

translations.literal: Because his elder brother Qin and Wei were old friends, he sent to win him over.
translations.idiomatic: Yu sent envoys to win Wei, citing his brother Qin's friendship with him.

sentences.zh: 頠不從，謂使曰：「高州昆季隆顯，莫非國恩，今應赴難援都，豈可自為跋扈。」

translations.literal: Wei refused and told the envoy, "The glory of the Gaozhou brothers is all the state's favor; now they should go to the capital's aid in time of danger. How can they make themselves domineering?"
translations.idiomatic: Wei refused and told the envoy, "The glory of the Gaozhou brothers is all the state's favor; now they should go to the capital's aid in time of danger. How can they make themselves domineering?"

sentences.zh: 及陳武帝入援都，將至始興，頠乃深自結托。

translations.literal: When Chen Baxian entered to relieve the capital and was about to reach Shixing, Wei then bound himself to him in deep trust.
translations.idiomatic: As Chen Baxian marched to relieve the capital and neared Shixing, Wei pledged himself wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 裕遣兵攻頠，武帝援之。

translations.literal: Yu sent troops to attack Wei; the Emperor aided him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu attacked; Chen Baxian sent aid.

sentences.zh: 裕敗，武帝以王懷明為衡州刺史，遷頠為始興內史。

translations.literal: Yu was defeated; the Emperor made Wang Huaiming inspector of Hengzhou and transferred Wei to interior governor of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was beaten; Chen Baxian named Wang Huaiming inspector of Hengzhou and moved Wei to interior governor of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 武帝之討蔡路養、李遷仕也，頠助帝平之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor campaigned against Cai Luzhai and Li Qianshi, Wei helped the emperor pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaigns against Cai Luzhai and Li Qianshi, Wei fought at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝承制以始興郡為東衡州，以頠為刺史，封新豐縣伯。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang, acting on imperial authority, made Shixing commandery East Hengzhou, appointed Wei its inspector, and enfeoffed him as Baron of Xinfeng county.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan, exercising regency powers, made Shixing into East Hengzhou, named Wei its inspector, and enfeoffed him as baron of Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 侯景平，元帝遍問朝宰，使各舉所知，群臣未對。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified, Emperor Yuan asked all the court ministers in turn, ordering each to recommend whom he knew; the assembled ministers had not yet replied.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing fell, Emperor Yuan asked the ministers, each to name men they knew. No one had answered yet.

sentences.zh: 元帝曰：「吾已得一人矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan said: "I have already obtained one man.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan said, "I already have one man.

sentences.zh: 歐陽頠甚公正，本有匡濟才，恐蕭廣州不肯致之。」

translations.literal: Ouyang Wei is very fair-minded and originally had talent to support and save the age, but I fear Xiao of Guangzhou will not be willing to send him."
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Wei is very fair-minded and originally had talent to support and save the age, but I fear Xiao of Guangzhou will not be willing to send him."

sentences.zh: 乃授武州刺史。

translations.literal: He then appointed him Inspector of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then made him inspector of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋授郢州，欲令出嶺，蕭勃留之，不獲拜命。

translations.literal: Soon he appointed Yingzhou, wishing to have him leave the mountains; Xiao Bo detained him and he could not take up the commission.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he named him to Yingzhou to draw him out of the hills. Xiao Bo held him fast and he never took office.

sentences.zh: 尋授衡州刺史，進封始興縣侯。

translations.literal: Soon he appointed him Inspector of Hengzhou and advanced his enfeoffment to Marquis of Shixing county.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made inspector of Hengzhou and advanced to marquis of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 時蕭勃在廣州，兵強位重，元帝深患之，遣王琳代為刺史。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Bo was at Guangzhou, troops strong and position weighty; Emperor Yuan deeply worried about him and sent Wang Lin to replace him as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Bo at Guangzhou was strong in troops and heavy in rank. Emperor Yuan feared him and sent Wang Lin to replace him.

sentences.zh: 琳已至小桂嶺，勃遣其將孫瑒監州，盡率部下至始興避琳兵鋒。

translations.literal: Lin had already reached Little Gui Ridge; Bo sent his general Sun Yu to oversee the province, led all his subordinates to Shixing, and avoided Lin's military edge.
translations.idiomatic: Lin had reached Little Gui Ridge. Bo sent Sun Yu to hold the province, drew all his men to Shixing, and shied from Lin's edge.

sentences.zh: 頠別據一城，不往謁勃，閉門高壘，亦不拒戰。

translations.literal: Wei separately held one city, did not go to call on Bo, shut the gates and piled high ramparts, and also did not resist in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wei held a separate city, would not call on Bo, shut the gates, piled the ramparts, and would not fight.

sentences.zh: 勃怒，遣兵襲頠，盡收其貲財馬仗。

translations.literal: Bo was angry and sent troops to strike Wei, seizing all his wealth, horses, and arms.
translations.idiomatic: Bo in rage sent troops and seized all his wealth, horses, and arms.

sentences.zh: 尋赦之，還復其所，復與結盟。

translations.literal: Soon he pardoned him, restored what was his, and again made alliance with him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he pardoned him, restored his goods, and swore alliance again.

sentences.zh: 魏平荊州，頠委質於勃。

translations.literal: When Wei pacified Jingzhou, Wei pledged himself to Bo.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei took Jingzhou, Wei pledged himself to Bo.

sentences.zh: 及勃度嶺出南康，以頠為前軍都督，周文育破禽之，送于武帝，帝釋而禮之。

translations.literal: When Bo crossed the range and came out to Nankang, he made Wei commander of the vanguard; Zhou Wenyü defeated and captured him and sent him to Chen Baxian; the Emperor released him and treated him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Bo crossed to Nankang and made Wei his vanguard. Zhou Wenyü broke and captured him and sent him to Chen Baxian, who freed him and received him graciously.

sentences.zh: 蕭勃死後，嶺南亂，頠有聲南土，且與武帝有舊，乃授安南將軍、衡州刺史，封始興縣侯。

translations.literal: After Xiao Bo died, south of the mountains was disturbed; Wei had a reputation in the southern lands, and moreover had old ties with Chen Baxian; he was then appointed Pacify-the-South General and Inspector of Hengzhou, enfeoffed as Marquis of Shixing county.
translations.idiomatic: After Bo died the south was in turmoil. Wei was famed there and was Chen Baxian's old friend—so he received pacify-the-south general, inspectorship of Hengzhou, and the marquisate of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 未至嶺，頠子紇已克始興。

translations.literal: Before he reached the ridge, Wei's son He had already taken Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Before he crossed the ridge, his son He had already taken Shixing.

sentences.zh: 及頠至，嶺南皆懾伏，仍進廣州，盡有越地。

translations.literal: When Wei arrived, all south of the mountains were awed and submitted; he still advanced to Guangzhou and wholly possessed the Yue lands.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, all south of the mountains submitted in awe. He pressed on to Guangzhou and held all Yue.

sentences.zh: 改授都督交廣等十九州諸軍事、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as Commander-in-Chief of military affairs of Jiao, Guang, and nineteen other provinces, General Who Pacifies Yue of the Center, and Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commander of nineteen provinces including Jiao and Guang, center-general who pacifies Yue, and inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 王琳據有中流，頠自海道及東嶺奉使不絕。

translations.literal: Wang Lin held the middle Yangzi; Wei by sea route and the eastern ridge sent envoys without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin held the middle river. Wei kept envoys moving by sea and the eastern passes.

sentences.zh: 永定三年，即本號開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongding, with his former title he was given Grand Precedence of the Palace equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongding he was given grand precedence with his old title.

sentences.zh: 文帝即位，進號征南將軍，改封陽山郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, his designation was advanced to General Who Campaigns South, and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Yangshan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded he was made general who campaigns south and Duke of Yangshan.

sentences.zh: 初，交州刺史袁曇緩密以金五百兩寄頠，令以百兩還合浦太守襲蒍，四百兩付兒智矩，餘人弗之知。

translations.literal: Earlier, Inspector of Jiaozhou Yuan Tanhuan had secretly deposited with Wei five hundred taels of gold, ordering one hundred taels returned to Administrator of Hepu Xi Cai, four hundred taels given to his son Zhiju—others did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yuan Tanhuan of Jiaozhi had secretly left Wei five hundred taels—one hundred for Hepu administrator Xi Cai, four hundred for his son Zhiju—unknown to anyone else.

sentences.zh: 頠尋為蕭勃所破，貲財並盡，唯所寄金獨存，曇緩亦尋卒，至是，頠並依信還之，時人莫不歎伏之。

translations.literal: Wei was soon broken by Xiao Bo and all wealth was exhausted; only the deposited gold remained alone. Tanhuan also soon died; at this Wei faithfully returned it all according to trust; men of the time all sighed in admiration of him.
translations.idiomatic: Bo soon broke him and stripped him bare—only the entrusted gold remained. Tanhuan died too. Wei returned every ounce faithfully, and men marveled.

sentences.zh: 時頠合門顯貴，威振南土，又多致銅鼓生口，獻奉珍異，前後委積，頗有助軍國。

translations.literal: At the time the whole house of Wei was illustrious and honored, awe-inspiring on the southern lands; they also repeatedly sent bronze drums and captives, presented rare tribute; before and after it piled up and greatly aided army and state.
translations.idiomatic: The whole Wei house stood high in the south. They sent bronze drums, captives, and rare tribute in heaps that greatly fed army and state.

sentences.zh: 天嘉四年薨，贈司空，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiancheng he died; posthumously made Minister of Works, posthumous title Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Tiancheng. Posthumously: minister of works, posthumous name Mu.

sentences.zh: 子紇嗣。

translations.literal: His son He succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son He succeeded.

sentences.zh: 紇字奉聖，頗有幹略，襲父官爵，在州十餘年，威惠著於百越。

translations.literal: He, styled Fengsheng, had considerable ability and strategy, inherited his father’s office and rank, and spent more than ten years in the province, where his authority and kindness were renowned among the Hundred Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He, styled Fengsheng, had considerable ability and strategy, inherited his father’s office and rank, and spent more than ten years in the province, where his authority and kindness were renowned among the Hundred Yue.

sentences.zh: 宣帝以紇久在南服，頗疑之。

translations.literal: Because He had long been in the southern dependencies, Emperor Xuan was rather suspicious of him.
translations.idiomatic: Because He had long been in the southern dependencies, Emperor Xuan was rather suspicious of him.

sentences.zh: 太建元年，徵為左衛將軍，其部下多勸之反，遂舉兵攻衡州刺史錢道戢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taijian, he was summoned to be General of the Left Guard; many of his subordinates urged him to rebel, and he accordingly raised troops and attacked Qian Daoji, inspector of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taijian, he was summoned to be General of the Left Guard; many of his subordinates urged him to rebel, and he accordingly raised troops and attacked Qian Daoji, inspector of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔儀同章昭達討禽之，送至都，伏誅。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yitong Zhang Zhaoda to campaign against and capture him; he was sent to the capital and executed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yitong Zhang Zhaoda to campaign against and capture him; he was sent to the capital and executed.

sentences.zh: 子詢以年幼免。

translations.literal: His son Xun was spared because he was young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun was spared because he was young.

sentences.zh: 黃法奭字仲昭，巴山新建人也。

translations.literal: Huang Fa, styled Zhongzhao, was a native of Xinjian in Bashan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Fa, styled Zhongzhao, came from Xinjian in Bashan.

sentences.zh: 少勁捷有膽力，日步行二百里，能距躍三丈。

translations.literal: In youth he was vigorous and swift, brave and strong; on foot he could cover two hundred li in a day and could leap three zhang in a bound.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was quick and fearless, could march two hundred li in a day on foot, and leap three zhang in a bound.

sentences.zh: 頗便書疏，閑明簿領，出入州郡中，為鄉閭所憚。

translations.literal: He was quite skilled at letters and memorials, clear and adept in registers and accounts; moving in and out among the prefectures and commanderies, the township and hamlets feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote well and kept accounts with ease. Moving through the prefectures and commanderies, he was feared in every village.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，於鄉里合徒眾。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing’s rebellion, Huang Fashi gathered followers in his home district.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing’s rebellion, Huang Fashi gathered followers in his home district.

sentences.zh: 太守賀詡下江州，法奭監知郡事。

translations.literal: When Governor He Xu went down to Jiangzhou, Fashi supervised commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor He Xu went down to Jiangzhou, Fashi supervised commandery affairs.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝將踰嶺入援建鄴，李遷仕作梗中途，武帝命周文育屯西昌，法奭遣兵助文育。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Chen was about to cross the passes to aid Jiankang, Li Qianshi obstructed the route, so Emperor Wu ordered Zhou Wenyu to garrison Xichang, and Fashi sent troops to aid Wenyu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Chen was about to cross the passes to aid Jiankang, Li Qianshi obstructed the route, so Emperor Wu ordered Zhou Wenyu to garrison Xichang, and Fashi sent troops to aid Wenyu.

sentences.zh: 時法奭出頓新淦縣，景遣行臺于慶來襲新淦，法奭敗之。

translations.literal: At the time Fashi went out and encamped at Xingan County; Hou Jing sent acting administrator Yu Qing to raid Xingan, and Fashi defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Fashi went out and encamped at Xingan County; Hou Jing sent acting administrator Yu Qing to raid Xingan, and Fashi defeated him.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝承制授交州刺史資，領新淦縣令，封巴山縣子。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang, acting under provisional authority, granted him the emoluments of inspector of Jiaozhou, made him concurrently magistrate of Xingan County, and enfeoffed him as Viscount of Bashan County.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang, acting under provisional authority, granted him the emoluments of inspector of Jiaozhou, made him concurrently magistrate of Xingan County, and enfeoffed him as Viscount of Bashan County.

sentences.zh: 敬帝即位，改封新建縣侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing took the throne, his enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Xinjian County.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing took the throne, his enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Xinjian County.

sentences.zh: 太平元年，割江州四郡置高州，以法奭為刺史，鎮巴山。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiping, four commanderies of Jiangzhou were carved off to establish Gaozhou; Fa was made inspector and garrisoned at Bashan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiping (556) four Jiangzhou commanderies were split off as Gaozhou. Fa was made inspector and garrisoned at Bashan.

sentences.zh: 蕭勃遣歐陽頠來攻，法奭破之。

translations.literal: Xiao Bo sent Ouyang Wei to attack; Fa defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Bo sent Ouyang Wei against him. Fa met him in battle and broke his force.

sentences.zh: 永定二年，王琳遣李孝欽、樊猛、餘孝頃攻周迪，且謀取法奭，法奭援迪，禽孝頃等三將。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongding, Wang Lin sent Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and Yu Xiaoxiang to attack Zhou Di and also plotted to take Fa; Fa aided Di and captured Xiaoxiang and three other generals.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongding (558) Wang Lin sent Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and Yu Xiaoxiang against Zhou Di and also meant to take Fa. Fa marched to Di's aid and captured Xiaoxiang and two other generals.

sentences.zh: 以功授平南將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed Pacify-the-South General and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was made pacify-the-south general and grand master with the gold seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 熊曇朗于金口害周文育，法奭共周迪討平之。

translations.literal: Xiong Tanlang at Jinkou killed Zhou Wenyü; Fa together with Zhou Di campaigned and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Tanlang killed Zhou Wenyü at Jinkou. Fa and Zhou Di crushed him.

sentences.zh: 天嘉三年，周迪反，法奭與吳明徹討平迪，法奭功居多。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancheng, Zhou Di rebelled; Fa together with Wu Mingche pacified Di; Fa's merit was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tiancheng (562) Zhou Di rebelled. Fa and Wu Mingche suppressed him, and Fa's merit stood first.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，進爵為公。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, he was advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne, Fa was raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 太建五年，大舉北侵，法奭為都督，出曆陽。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taijian, a great northern invasion was launched; Fa was made area commander and went out from Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taijian (573) a great northern campaign was launched. Fa was made area commander and advanced from Liyang.

sentences.zh: 於是為拋車及步艦，豎拍以逼之，炮加其樓堞，克之，盡誅其戍卒。

translations.literal: Thereupon they built battering carts and foot warships, erected pounders to press on them, applied cannon to their towers and battlements, took it, and put all garrison troops to death.
translations.idiomatic: They built battering carts and foot warships, drove the rams against the walls, and brought cannon to bear on the towers. The city fell and every man in the garrison was killed.

sentences.zh: 進兵合肥，望旗降款。

translations.literal: Advancing troops to Hefei, they surrendered at sight of the standards.
translations.idiomatic: At Hefei they surrendered at the first sight of his banners.

sentences.zh: 法奭禁侵掠，躬自勞撫而與之盟，並放還北。

translations.literal: Fa forbade plundering, personally went among them to comfort and soothe, made covenant with them, and sent them all back north.
translations.idiomatic: Fa forbade plunder, comforted them himself, made covenant, and sent them all back north.

sentences.zh: 以功加侍中，改封義陽郡公。

translations.literal: For merit he was given additional appointment as Palace Attendant and his enfeoffment changed to Duke of Yiyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was made palace attendant as well and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 七年，為豫州刺史，鎮壽陽。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was made Inspector of Yuzhou and garrisoned at Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made inspector of Yuzhou and garrisoned at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈司空，諡曰威。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Minister of Works, posthumous name Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He died. Posthumously: minister of works, posthumous name Wei.

sentences.zh: 子玩嗣。

translations.literal: His son Wan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 淳於量字思明，其先濟北人也。

translations.literal: Chun Yuliang, styled Siming; his ancestors were natives of Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: Chun Yuliang, styled Siming, came from Jibei stock.

sentences.zh: 世居建鄴。

translations.literal: For generations they dwelt at Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family had lived at Jianye.

sentences.zh: 父文成，仕梁為將帥，位梁州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Wencheng served Liang as a general and rose to Inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wencheng served Liang as a commander and rose to inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 量少善自居處，偉姿容，有幹略，便弓馬。

translations.literal: In youth Liang was good at deporting himself, of imposing looks, possessed of capacity and strategy, skilled at bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Yuliang carried himself well, had a commanding presence, showed judgment and resolve, and fought well from horseback.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝為荊州刺史，文成分量人馬，令往事焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang was Inspector of Jingzhou, Wencheng assigned Liang men and horses and ordered him to serve there.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Liang governed Jingzhou, Wencheng gave Yuliang troops and horses and sent him to serve there.

sentences.zh: 以軍功封廣晉縣男。

translations.literal: For military merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Guangjin.
translations.idiomatic: For military merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Guangjin.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，梁元帝凡遣五軍入援臺，量預其一。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion, Emperor Yuan of Liang in all sent five armies to enter and relieve the Terrace City; Liang participated in one of them.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion Emperor Yuan of Liang sent five armies to relieve the Terrace City. Yuliang served in one of them.

sentences.zh: 臺城陷，量還荊州。

translations.literal: When the Terrace City fell, Liang returned to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Terrace City fell, Yuliang returned to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 元帝承制以為巴州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan under the provisional mandate appointed him Inspector of Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan, acting under the provisional mandate, made him inspector of Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 侯景西上攻巴州，元帝使都督王僧辯入據巴陵，量與僧辯並力拒景，大敗之，禽其將任約。

translations.literal: Hou Jing attacked Bazhou from the west; Emperor Yuan sent area commander Wang Sengbian to enter and hold Baling; Liang together with Sengbian joined strength to resist Jing, inflicted a great defeat, and captured his general Ren Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing attacked Bazhou from the west. Emperor Yuan sent Wang Sengbian to hold Baling. Yuliang and Sengbian joined forces, shattered Jing's army, and captured his general Ren Yue.

sentences.zh: 進攻郢州，獲宋子仙。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Yingzhou, they captured Song Zixian.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing on to Yingzhou, they took Song Zixian.

sentences.zh: 仍隨僧辯平侯景。

translations.literal: He still followed Sengbian in pacifying Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Sengbian in suppressing Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 封謝沐縣侯。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiemu county.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as marquis of Xiemu.

sentences.zh: 尋出為都督、桂州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as area commander and Inspector of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he went out as area commander and inspector of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 及魏克荊州，量保桂州。

translations.literal: When Wei took Jingzhou, Liang held and defended Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei took Jingzhou, Yuliang held Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 王琳擁割湘、郢，累遣召量，量外雖與琳往來，而別遣使歸陳武帝。

translations.literal: Wang Lin held and carved up Xiang and Ying; he repeatedly sent summonses to Liang; outwardly Liang kept dealings with Lin, but separately he sent envoys to return to Chen Baxian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin held Xiang and Ying and repeatedly summoned Yuliang. Outwardly Yuliang dealt with Lin, but in secret he sent envoys to Chen Baxian.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，進位鎮西大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Chen Baxian received the abdication, he was advanced in position to Secure-the-West Grand General and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Baxian took the throne, Yuliang was made secure-the-west grand general and grand master with the gold seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 天嘉五年，徵為中撫軍大將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tiancheng he was summoned as Central Pacification Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tiancheng (564) he was recalled as central pacification grand general.

sentences.zh: 量所部將率多戀本土，並欲逃入山谷，不願入朝。

translations.literal: The generals and commanders under Liang's command for the most part longed for their native lands, and all wished to flee into mountain valleys and would not come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the generals under Yuliang longed for home. They meant to flee into the hills rather than go to court.

sentences.zh: 文帝使湘州刺史華皎征衡州，且以兵迎量。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen sent Inspector of Xiangzhou Hua Jiao to campaign against Hengzhou and also to bring troops to receive Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen sent Hua Jiao, inspector of Xiangzhou, to campaign in Hengzhou and also to bring troops to escort Yuliang in.

sentences.zh: 天康元年，至都，以在道淹留，為有司奏，免儀同，餘如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiankang he reached the capital; because of delay on the road he was impeached by the relevant office, stripped of grand-master status, the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiankang (566) he reached the capital. Because he had lingered on the road the authorities impeached him and stripped his grand-master rank, leaving the rest unchanged.

sentences.zh: 華皎構逆，以量為征南大將軍、西討大都督，總率大艦，自郢州樊浦拒之。

translations.literal: Hua Jiao plotted treason; Liang was made Campaign-the-South Grand General and Grand Commander of the Western Expedition, in overall command of great ships from Yingzhou's Fan Ford to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hua Jiao rebelled, Yuliang was made campaign-south grand general and grand commander of the western expedition, leading great ships from Yingzhou's Fan Ford against him.

sentences.zh: 皎平，並降周將長湖西元定等。

translations.literal: When Hua Jiao was pacified, he also forced the Zhou generals Zhanghu Xi Yuanding and others to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Hua Jiao was pacified, he also forced the Zhou generals Zhanghu Xi Yuanding and others to surrender.

sentences.zh: 以功授侍中、中軍大將軍、開府儀同三司，進封醴陵縣公。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed Palace Attendant, Central Army Grand General, and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Liling county.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was made palace attendant, central army grand general, and grand master with the gold seal and purple ribbon, and raised to Duke of Liling.

sentences.zh: 未拜，出為南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Before he took up the appointment he went out as Inspector of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take office he went out as inspector of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 太建元年，進號征北大將軍，給扶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taijian his designation was advanced to Campaign-North Grand General and he was given a crutch.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taijian (569) his title was raised to campaign-north grand general and he was given a crutch.

sentences.zh: 三年，就江陰王蕭季卿買梁陵中樹，季卿坐免，量免侍中。

translations.literal: In the third year, for buying trees from the Liang mausoleums together with the Prince of Jiangyin Xiao Jiqing, Jiqing was stripped of office and Liang was stripped of palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he and the Prince of Jiangyin, Xiao Jiqing, were found to have bought timber from the Liang imperial tombs. Jiqing was dismissed and Yuliang lost his palace attendant post.

sentences.zh: 尋復侍中。

translations.literal: Soon he was again palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made palace attendant again.

sentences.zh: 吳明徹之北侵也，量贊成其事。

translations.literal: At the time of Wu Mingche's northern invasion, Liang endorsed the undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Mingche marched north, Yuliang backed the campaign.

sentences.zh: 又遣第六子岑率所領從軍。

translations.literal: He also sent his sixth son Cen at the head of his command to follow the army.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent his sixth son Cen at the head of his own troops.

sentences.zh: 淮南克定，量改封始安郡公。

translations.literal: When the Huai River region was taken and settled, Liang's enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Shi'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huai region was pacified, Yuliang was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Shi'an.

sentences.zh: 及周獲吳明徹，乃以量為都督水陸諸軍事、車騎將軍、都督、南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zhou captured Wu Mingche, Liang was then made area commander of all land and water military affairs, Chariots-and-Cavalry General, area commander, and Inspector of South Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou captured Wu Mingche, Yuliang was made commander of all land and water forces, chariots-and-cavalry general, area commander, and inspector of South Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 十四年薨，贈司空。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died; posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he died. He was posthumously made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 章昭達字伯通，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhaoda, styled Botong, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhaoda, styled Botong, came from Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 性倜儻，輕財尚氣。

translations.literal: By nature he was unconventional, lightly valued wealth and prized bold spirit.
translations.idiomatic: He was free-spirited by nature, cared little for money, and prized boldness.

sentences.zh: 少時，遇相者謂曰：「卿容貌甚善，須小虧，則當富貴。」

translations.literal: In youth he met a physiognomist who told him, "Your appearance is very fine; if it suffers a small flaw, then you will become wealthy and honored."
translations.idiomatic: In youth he met a physiognomist who told him, "Your appearance is very fine; if it suffers a small flaw, then you will become wealthy and honored."

sentences.zh: 梁大同中，昭達為東宮直後，因醉墯馬，鬢角小傷，昭達喜之，相者曰：「未也。」

translations.literal: In the Datong era of Liang, Zhaoda was direct attendant behind the Eastern Palace; drunk he fell from a horse and received a small wound at the temple; Zhaoda was pleased at this; the physiognomist said, "Not yet."
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang's Datong reign he was direct attendant to the Eastern Palace. Drunk, he fell from his horse and cut his temple. Zhaoda was pleased. The physiognomist said, "Not yet."

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，昭達率鄉人援臺，為流矢所中，眇其一目。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Zhaoda led his native district to aid the Terrace City; he was struck by a stray arrow and lost sight in one eye.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion he led home recruits to relieve the Terrace City. A stray arrow blinded one eye.

sentences.zh: 相者見之，曰：「卿相善矣，不久當富貴。」

translations.literal: The physiognomist saw him and said: "Your physiognomy is now excellent; before long you will be ennobled."
translations.idiomatic: The physiognomist saw him and said, "Now your fate is set. You will soon be ennobled."

sentences.zh: 臺城陷，昭達還鄉里，與陳文帝遊，因結君臣分。

translations.literal: When the Terrace City fell, Zhaoda returned to his native place and associated with Emperor Wen; thereby they formed the distinction of lord and minister.
translations.idiomatic: When the Terrace City fell he went home and fell in with Emperor Wen, and from that day they were lord and minister.

sentences.zh: 侯景平，文帝為吳興太守，昭達杖策來謁。

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified, Emperor Wen was Administrator of Wuxing; Zhaoda came leaning on his staff to call on him.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing fell, Emperor Wen became administrator of Wuxing. Zhaoda came leaning on his staff to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 文帝見之大喜，因委以將帥，恩寵超於儕等。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen saw him he was greatly pleased and therefore entrusted him with command of troops; favor and grace surpassing his peers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was delighted and put him in command of troops, favoring him above his peers.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝謀討王僧辯，令文帝還長城招聚兵眾，以備杜龕，頻使昭達往京口稟承計畫。

translations.literal: When Chen Baxian plotted to campaign against Wang Sengbian, he ordered Emperor Wen to return to Changcheng to gather troops and supplies against Du Kan, and repeatedly sent Zhaoda to Jingkou to receive and carry out plans.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Baxian moved against Wang Sengbian he sent Emperor Wen back to Changcheng to raise men and stores against Du Kan and repeatedly sent Zhaoda to Jingkou to carry his orders.

sentences.zh: 僧辯誅後，杜龕遣其將杜泰來攻長城，昭達因從文帝進軍吳興以討龕。

translations.literal: After Sengbian was executed, Du Kan sent his general Du Tai to attack Changcheng; Zhaoda then followed Emperor Wen in advancing the army to Wuxing to campaign against Kan.
translations.idiomatic: After Sengbian was killed, Kan sent Du Tai against Changcheng. Zhaoda followed Emperor Wen east and marched on Wuxing to attack Kan.

sentences.zh: 龕平，又從討張彪於會稽，克之。

translations.literal: When Kan was pacified, he again followed in campaigning against Zhang Biao at Kuaiji and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: When Kan fell he marched again with Emperor Wen against Zhang Biao at Kuaiji and took the city.

sentences.zh: 累功除定州刺史。

translations.literal: For accumulated merit he was appointed Inspector of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For accumulated merit he was made inspector of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時留異擁據東陽，武帝患之，乃使昭達為長山令，居其心腹。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Yi held Dongyang in his grip; Chen Baxian was troubled by it and therefore made Zhaoda magistrate of Changshan county, placing him in Yi's heartland.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Yi held Dongyang. Chen Baxian, troubled by this, made Zhaoda magistrate of Changshan county to plant him in Yi's heartland.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，追論長城功，封欣樂縣侯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng, for merit at the defense of Changcheng he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xinle county.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiancheng (562), for merit at Changcheng he was enfeoffed as marquis of Xinle.

sentences.zh: 尋隨侯安都拒王琳，昭達乘平虜大艦，中流而進，先鋒發拍，中賊艦。

translations.literal: Soon he followed Hou Andu in resisting Wang Lin; Zhaoda rode the Flat-Barbarian great ship, advanced midstream, and the vanguard's pounders struck the rebel ships.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he followed Hou Andu against Wang Lin. Zhaoda sailed the Flat-Barbarian great ship midstream; the vanguard's pounders struck the rebel ships.

sentences.zh: 王琳平，昭達策勳第一。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin was pacified, Zhaoda's registered merit ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lin was suppressed, Zhaoda's merit was entered first on the rolls.

sentences.zh: 二年，除都督、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year he was made area commander and Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made area commander and inspector of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 周迪據臨川反，詔昭達便道征之。

translations.literal: Zhou Di held Linchuan in rebellion; an edict ordered Zhaoda to campaign against him by convenient route.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Di rebelled in Linchuan; an edict sent Zhaoda against him by the direct route.

sentences.zh: 迪敗走，徵為護軍將軍，改封邵武縣侯。

translations.literal: When Di was defeated and fled, he was summoned as Protector General and his enfeoffment changed to Marquis of Shaowu county.
translations.idiomatic: When Di was beaten and fled, Zhaoda was recalled as protector general and re-enfeoffed as marquis of Shaowu.

sentences.zh: 四年，陳寶應納周迪，共寇臨川，又以昭達為都督討迪。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Chen Baoying took Zhou Di in and together they raided Linchuan again; Zhaoda was again made area commander to campaign against Di.
translations.idiomatic: In year four Chen Baoying sheltered Zhou Di and they raided Linchuan again; Zhaoda was again made area commander against Di.

sentences.zh: 迪走，昭達乃踰嶺討陳寶應。

translations.literal: Di fled; Zhaoda then crossed the ranges to campaign against Chen Baoying.
translations.idiomatic: Di fled. Zhaoda then crossed the mountains to march against Chen Baoying.

sentences.zh: 與戰不利，因據上流為筏，施拍其上，壞其水柵。

translations.literal: He fought without success and therefore held the upper reaches, built rafts, mounted pounders on them, and destroyed their water stockades.
translations.idiomatic: He fought without success, then held the upper river, built rafts, mounted pounders on them, and smashed their water stockades.

sentences.zh: 又出兵攻其步軍。

translations.literal: He also sent troops out to attack their infantry.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent troops to attack their infantry.

sentences.zh: 方大合戰，會文帝遣余孝頃出自海道，適至，因並力乘之，遂定閩中，盡禽留異、寶應。

translations.literal: Just as the great combined battle was underway, it happened that Emperor Wen had sent Yu Xiaoxiang out by the sea route; he arrived at that moment, and therefore with combined strength they pressed the attack, and thereby pacified Minzhong, capturing Liu Yi and Chen Baoying entirely.
translations.idiomatic: As the great battle was joining, Yu Xiaoxiang—the force Emperor Wen had sent by sea—arrived at exactly the right moment. Together they pressed the attack, pacified Minzhong, and took Liu Yi and Chen Baoying alive.

sentences.zh: 以功授鎮軍將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and given the privilege of an office equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: For this merit he was made General Who Pacifies the Army with privilege equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 初，文帝嘗夢昭達升台鉉，及旦，以夢告之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Wen had once dreamed that Zhaoda ascended to the platform and wore the minister's ring; at dawn he told him the dream.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Emperor Wen had dreamed that Zhaoda mounted the platform and took up the minister's ring. At dawn he told him the dream.

sentences.zh: 至是，侍宴酒酣，顧昭達曰：「卿憶夢不？

translations.literal: At this time, while attending a banquet and deep in wine, he turned to Zhaoda and said: "Do you recall the dream?
translations.idiomatic: Now, over wine at a banquet, he turned to Zhaoda and said, "Do you remember the dream?

sentences.zh: 何以償夢？」

translations.literal: How will you repay the dream?"
translations.idiomatic: How will you repay it?"

sentences.zh: 昭達對曰：「當效犬馬之用，以盡臣節，自餘無以奉償。」

translations.literal: Zhaoda answered, "I shall offer the service of a dog or horse, exhausting a minister's duty; beyond that, I have no way to repay you."
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoda answered, "I shall offer the service of a dog or horse, exhausting a minister's duty; beyond that, I have no way to repay you."

sentences.zh: 尋出為都督、江州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as area commander and Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was posted out as area commander and inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，改封邵陵郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Fei ascended, his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of the Commandery of Shaoling.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Fei came to the throne, he was refeudated as Duke of Shaoling commandery.

sentences.zh: 華皎之反，其移文並假以昭達為辭，又頻遣使招之，昭達盡執其使送都。

translations.literal: In Hua Jiao's rebellion, his proclamations all cited Zhaoda as a pretext, and he repeatedly sent envoys to recruit him; Zhaoda seized all his envoys and sent them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Hua Jiao rebelled, his manifestos cited Zhaoda as pretext, and he repeatedly sent envoys to win him over. Zhaoda seized every envoy and sent them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，徵為中撫大將軍。

translations.literal: When his term expired he was summoned as Grand General Who Calms the Center.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was recalled as Grand General Who Calms the Center.

sentences.zh: 宣帝即位，進號車騎大將軍，以還朝遲留，為有司所劾，降號車騎將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan ascended, his title was advanced to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry; because his return to court was delayed and prolonged, he was impeached by the relevant offices and his title was reduced to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan took the throne Zhaoda was promoted to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, but because he lingered on the road returning to court the relevant offices impeached him and he was reduced to General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 歐陽紇據嶺南反，詔昭達都督眾軍征之。
