translations.literal: Ouyang He held the Lingnan and rebelled; an edict ordered Zhaoda to command all armies to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang He rebelled and held Lingnan. An edict put Zhaoda in command of all forces against him.

sentences.zh: 紇聞昭達奄至，乃出頓洭口，聚沙石，盛以竹籠，置於水柵之外，用遏舟艦。

translations.literal: He heard that Zhaoda had suddenly arrived; he then came out and halted at Huangkou, gathered sand and stone, filled bamboo cages with them, and placed them outside the water stockade to obstruct warships.
translations.idiomatic: When He heard that Zhaoda had appeared suddenly, he marched out and encamped at Huangkou. He piled sand and stone into bamboo cages and set them outside his water stockade to block the fleet.

sentences.zh: 昭達居其上流，裝艦造拍，以臨賊柵。

translations.literal: Zhaoda occupied the upper reaches, fitted out ships and built pounders, to press upon the rebel stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoda held the upper river, fitted out ships, and built pounders to bear on the rebel stockade.

sentences.zh: 又令人銜刀潛行水中，以斫竹籠，籠篾皆解。

translations.literal: He also had men hold knives in their mouths and steal through the water to cut the bamboo cages; the strips of the cages all came apart.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent men with knives gripped in their teeth to swim under the water and cut the bamboo cages apart.

sentences.zh: 因縱大艦突之，大敗紇，禽之送都。

translations.literal: He then unleashed great ships to storm them, greatly defeated He, captured him and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Then he drove his great ships in and routed He, captured him, and sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 廣州平，進位司空。

translations.literal: When Guangzhou was pacified, he advanced in rank to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzhou was pacified he was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 太建二年，征江陵。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taijian, he campaigned against Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taijian (570) he marched against Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 時梁明帝與周軍大蓄舟艦於青泥中，昭達分遣偏將錢道戢、程文季乘輕舟焚之。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Ming of Liang and the Zhou army had greatly stored boats and ships in Qingni; Zhaoda separately dispatched subordinate generals Qian Daoji and Cheng Wenji to ride light boats and burn them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Liang and the Zhou forces had massed boats at Qingni. Zhaoda detached Qian Daoji and Cheng Wenji with light craft to burn them.

sentences.zh: 周又于峽口南岸築壘，名安蜀城，于江上橫引大索，編葦為橋，以度軍糧。

translations.literal: Zhou also built a fortress on the south bank of the gorge mouth, named Pacify Shu Fortress; across the river they stretched great cables, wove reeds into a bridge, to convey army grain.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou also built a fort on the south bank at the gorge mouth, called Pacify Shu Fortress, stretched great cables across the river, and wove a reed bridge to convoy army grain.

sentences.zh: 昭達乃命軍士為長戟，施樓船上，仰割其索。

translations.literal: Zhaoda then ordered the soldiers to make long halberds, mount them on tower ships, and cut the cables from below looking up.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoda had his men forge long halberds, mount them on tower ships, and reach up to cut the cables.

sentences.zh: 索斷糧絕，因縱兵攻其城，降之。

translations.literal: When the cables broke grain supply ceased; he then unleashed troops to attack their fortress and accepted its surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The cables broke and the grain line failed. He then stormed the fort and took its surrender.

sentences.zh: 三年，於軍中病薨，贈大將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year he died of illness in the army; posthumously he was given Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he died of illness in camp and was posthumously made Grand General.

sentences.zh: 昭達性嚴刻，每奉命出征，必晝夜倍道；

translations.literal: Zhaoda's nature was severe and exacting; whenever he received orders to campaign he invariably marched day and night at double pace;
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoda was severe by nature. Whenever he took the field he marched day and night at forced pace;

sentences.zh: 然其所克，必推功將帥。

translations.literal: yet in what he conquered he invariably attributed merit to his commanders and generals.
translations.idiomatic: yet whatever he won he credited to his commanders.

sentences.zh: 廚膳飲食，並同群下，將士亦以此附之。

translations.literal: Kitchen fare and drink were all the same as those below; officers and soldiers also for this reason attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: He ate and drank what his men ate and drank, and they followed him for it.

sentences.zh: 每飲會，必盛設女伎雜樂，備羌、胡之聲，音律姿容，並一時之妙，雖臨敵弗之廢也。

translations.literal: At every drinking gathering he invariably set out female performers and mixed music in profusion, including Qiang and Hu sounds; music, bearing, and beauty were all the finest of the age—even when facing the enemy he did not abandon it.
translations.idiomatic: At every feast he staged female musicians and mixed ensembles with Qiang and Hu music, all matchless in skill and beauty—and he never gave them up even on campaign.

sentences.zh: 四年，配享文帝廟庭。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was allotted share in sacrifice in Emperor Wen's temple courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he was granted co-worship in Emperor Wen's temple.

sentences.zh: 子大寶，襲邵陵郡公，位豐州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Dabao inherited the Duke of Shaoling commandery and held the post of Inspector of Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dabao inherited the dukedom of Shaoling and served as inspector of Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 在州貪縱，百姓怨酷，後主乙太僕卿李暈代之，乃襲殺暈而反。

translations.literal: In the province he was greedy and unrestrained; the people resented him bitterly. The Last Emperor replaced him with Grand Master of Servants Li Yun; he then ambushed and killed Yun and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was greedy and violent, and the people hated him. The Last Emperor replaced him with Grand Master of Servants Li Yun; Dabao ambushed and killed Yun and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 尋被禽，梟首朱雀航，夷三族。

translations.literal: Soon he was captured; his head was displayed at the Zhuque pontoon; his three clans were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon taken, his head hung at Zhuque pontoon, and his clans to the third degree were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 吳明徹字通照，秦郡人也。

translations.literal: Wu Mingche, styled Tongzhao, was a native of Qin commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mingche, styled Tongzhao, was from Qin commandery.

sentences.zh: 父樹，梁右軍將軍。

translations.literal: His father Shu was General of the Right Army under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shu had been Liang's General of the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 明徹幼孤，性至孝。

translations.literal: Mingche was orphaned young; his nature was utterly filial.
translations.idiomatic: Mingche lost his father young and was profoundly filial.

sentences.zh: 年十四，感墳塋未修，家貧無以取給，乃勤力耕種。

translations.literal: At age fourteen, moved that the tomb mound was not yet repaired and the family was poor with no means to provide, he labored diligently at planting.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen, troubled that the family tombs were unrepaired and too poor to afford it, he turned to hard farming.

sentences.zh: 時天下亢旱，苗稼焦枯，明徹哀憤，每之田中號哭，仰天自訴。

translations.literal: At that time throughout the realm there was severe drought; seedling crops were scorched dry; Mingche grieved in anger; each time he went to the fields he wailed, appealing to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce drought withered the crops. Mingche wept in the fields and cried out to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 居數日，有自田還者，雲苗已更生，明徹疑其紿己，及往如言，秋而大獲，足充葬用。

translations.literal: After several days someone returning from the fields said the seedlings had sprung anew; Mingche suspected he was deceiving him; when he went it was as said; in autumn there was a great harvest, enough to meet burial expenses.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later a neighbor said the shoots had greened again. Mingche did not believe it until he saw for himself. That autumn's harvest paid for the burial.

sentences.zh: 時有伊氏者，善占墓，謂其兄曰：「君葬日，必有乘白馬逐鹿者經墳，此是最小孝子大貴之征。」

translations.literal: At the time there was a man of the Yi clan who was skilled at divining graves. He told his elder brother, "On the day you are buried, someone riding a white horse and chasing a deer will surely pass the grave; this is the sign that the youngest filial son will become greatly honored."
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was a man of the Yi clan who was skilled at divining graves. He told his elder brother, "On the day you are buried, someone riding a white horse and chasing a deer will surely pass the grave; this is the sign that the youngest filial son will become greatly honored."

sentences.zh: 至時果有應。

translations.literal: When the time came it indeed came to pass.
translations.idiomatic: When the day came, it happened exactly so.

sentences.zh: 明徹即樹之小子也。

translations.literal: Mingche was precisely the youngest son of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Mingche was indeed Shu's youngest son.

sentences.zh: 及侯景寇都，明徹有粟麥三千餘斛，而鄰里饑餧，乃白諸兄曰：「今人不圖久，奈何不與鄉里共此。」

translations.literal: When Hou Jing attacked the capital, Mingche had more than three thousand hu of millet and wheat while his neighbors were starving, so he said to his elder brothers, "People now cannot plan for the long term; how can we not share this with our fellow villagers?"
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing attacked the capital, Mingche had more than three thousand hu of millet and wheat while his neighbors were starving, so he said to his elder brothers, "People now cannot plan for the long term; how can we not share this with our fellow villagers?"

sentences.zh: 於是計口平分，同其豐儉，群盜聞而避焉，賴以存者甚眾。

translations.literal: Thereupon they counted mouths and divided equally, sharing alike in plenty or want; bandits on hearing avoided the place; those who survived by this reliance were very many.
translations.idiomatic: They divided by headcount, rich and poor alike. Bandits heard of it and stayed away, and many lived because of them.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝鎮京口，深相要結，明徹乃詣武帝，帝為之降階，執手即席。

translations.literal: When Chen Baxian was garrisoning Jingkou he deeply sought his company; Mingche then went to call on the Emperor; the Emperor for his sake descended the steps, took his hand, and seated him at once.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Baxian held Jingkou he sought Mingche's friendship. Mingche came to call, and Baxian came down the steps, took his hand, and seated him at once.

sentences.zh: 明徹亦微涉書史經傳，就汝南周弘正學天文、孤虛、遁甲，略通其術，頗以英雄自許，武帝亦深奇之。

translations.literal: Mingche also lightly dipped into books, histories, and classic texts; he studied under Zhou Hongzheng of Runan in astronomy, void-and-solid divination, and Dunjia, and broadly mastered their arts; he somewhat styled himself a hero; the Emperor also deeply marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Mingche had some learning in the classics and studied astronomy, void-solid divination, and Dunjia under Zhou Hongzheng of Runan. He reckoned himself a man of heroic mold, and Baxian thought highly of him.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，授安南將軍，與侯安都、周文育將兵討王琳。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South; with Hou Andou and Zhou Wenyu he led troops to campaign against Wang Lin.
translations.idiomatic: When Baxian took the throne he made Mingche General Who Pacifies the South and sent him with Hou Andou and Zhou Wenyu against Wang Lin.

sentences.zh: 及眾軍敗沒，明徹自拔還都。

translations.literal: When the armies were defeated and lost, Mingche cut his own way out and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies were wiped out Mingche fought his way back to the capital alone.

sentences.zh: 文帝即位，以本官加右衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Mingche retained his current office and was additionally made General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Mingche retained his current office and was additionally made General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 及周迪反，詔以明徹為江州刺史，領豫章太守，總眾軍以討迪。

translations.literal: When Zhou Di rebelled, an edict made Mingche inspector of Jiangzhou, concurrently governor of Yuzhang, and placed him in overall command of the armies to campaign against Di.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Di rebelled, an edict made Mingche inspector of Jiangzhou, concurrently governor of Yuzhang, and placed him in overall command of the armies to campaign against Di.

sentences.zh: 明徹雅性剛直，統內不甚和，文帝聞之，遣安成王頊代明徹，令以本號還朝。

translations.literal: Mingche’s nature was usually firm and upright, and those under his command were not very harmonious; when Emperor Wen heard this, he sent Xu, Prince of Ancheng, to replace Mingche and ordered Mingche to return to court with his original title.
translations.idiomatic: Mingche’s nature was usually firm and upright, and those under his command were not very harmonious; when Emperor Wen heard this, he sent Xu, Prince of Ancheng, to replace Mingche and ordered Mingche to return to court with his original title.

sentences.zh: 天嘉五年，遷吳興太守。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianjia, he was transferred to governor of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianjia, he was transferred to governor of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 及引辭之郡，帝謂曰：「吳興雖郡，帝鄉之重，故以相授。」

translations.literal: When he took leave to go to the commandery, the emperor said to him, “Although Wuxing is a commandery, it has the importance of the imperial home district, and therefore I entrust it to you.”
translations.idiomatic: When he took leave to go to the commandery, the emperor said to him, “Although Wuxing is a commandery, it has the importance of the imperial home district, and therefore I entrust it to you.”

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，授領軍將軍，尋遷丹陽尹，仍詔以甲仗四十人出入殿省。

translations.literal: When Emperor Fei ascended he was appointed General of the Palace Guard; soon he was moved to Intendant of Danyang; an edict additionally granted forty armored guards to accompany him in and out of the palace offices.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Fei made him General of the Palace Guard, then intendant of Danyang, with forty armored guards to accompany him in and out of the palace.

sentences.zh: 到仲舉之矯令出宣帝也，毛喜知其詐，宣帝懼，遣喜與明徹籌焉。

translations.literal: When Dao Zhongju forged an edict to send Emperor Xuan out, Mao Xi knew it was deceit; Emperor Xuan was afraid and sent Xi with Mingche to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: When Dao Zhongju forged orders to expel Emperor Xuan, Mao Xi saw through the fraud. Xuan was frightened and sent Xi to consult Mingche.

sentences.zh: 明徹曰：「嗣君諒闇，萬機多闕，殿下親實周、召，德冠伊、霍，願留中深計，慎勿致疑。」

translations.literal: Mingche said, "The succeeding ruler is in mourning seclusion, and the myriad affairs of state have many gaps. Your Highness is truly kin like the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao, and in virtue surpasses Yi Yin and Huo Guang. I hope you will remain within the palace and plan deeply; be careful not to cause suspicion."
translations.idiomatic: Mingche said, "The succeeding ruler is in mourning seclusion, and the myriad affairs of state have many gaps. Your Highness is truly kin like the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao, and in virtue surpasses Yi Yin and Huo Guang. I hope you will remain within the palace and plan deeply; be careful not to cause suspicion."

sentences.zh: 及湘州刺史華皎陰有異志，詔授明徹都督、湘州刺史，仍與征南大將軍淳于量等討皎。

translations.literal: When the Inspector of Xiangzhou Hua Jiao secretly harbored contrary intent, an edict appointed Mingche area commander and Inspector of Xiangzhou; he still joined Grand General Who Campaigns South Chunyu Liang and others to campaign against Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangzhou inspector Hua Jiao turned disloyal, an edict made Mingche area commander and Xiangzhou inspector, and he joined Grand General Who Campaigns South Chunyu Liang and others against Jiao.

sentences.zh: 皎平，授開府儀同三司，進爵為公。

translations.literal: When Jiao was pacified, he was given office equal to the Three Dukes and advanced in noble rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiao fell he received privilege equal to the Three Dukes and was ennobled as a duke.

sentences.zh: 太建五年，朝議北征，公卿互有異同，明徹決策請行。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taijian the court debated a northern campaign; dukes and ministers differed among themselves; Mingche resolved the decision and requested to go.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taijian (573) the court debated invading the north. Ministers were divided, but Mingche pressed to lead the campaign.

sentences.zh: 詔加侍中、都督征討諸軍事，總眾軍十餘萬發都，緣江城鎮，相續降款。

translations.literal: An edict added Palace Attendant and Commander Who Campaigns and Pacifies All Military Affairs; he gathered more than a hundred thousand troops and set out from the capital; along the Yangzi, cities and garrisons one after another submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was made palace attendant and supreme commander, mustered more than a hundred thousand men, and marched from the capital. Yangzi towns surrendered in succession.

sentences.zh: 軍至秦郡，齊大將軍尉破胡將兵為援，破走之，秦郡降。

translations.literal: The army reached Qin commandery; the Qi Grand General Wei Pohu led troops as relief; he routed and drove him off; Qin commandery surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: At Qin commandery Qi grand general Wei Pohu came to relieve the city. Mingche routed him and Qin surrendered.

sentences.zh: 宣帝以秦郡明徹舊邑，詔具太牢，令拜祠上塚，文武羽儀甚盛，鄉里榮之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan, because Qin commandery was Mingche's old district, ordered the full great offering sacrifice, directed him to worship at the shrine and ascend the tomb; civil and military display was very grand; the native place was honored.
translations.idiomatic: Qin was Mingche's home. Emperor Xuan ordered the full sacrificial beast, had him worship at his ancestral shrine and tomb, and sent him home in state so grand that his countrymen glowed with pride.

sentences.zh: 進克仁州。

translations.literal: He advanced and captured Renzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He took Renzhou.

sentences.zh: 授征北大將軍，進封南平郡公。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand General Who Campaigns North and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Nanping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand General Who Campaigns North and enfeoffed as Duke of Nanping commandery.

sentences.zh: 進逼壽陽，齊遣王琳拒守，明徹乘夜攻之，中宵而潰。

translations.literal: He advanced and pressed Shouyang; Qi sent Wang Lin to hold and defend; Mingche attacked by night; at midnight they broke.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed Shouyang. Qi sent Wang Lin to hold it. Mingche attacked at night and broke the defense by midnight.

sentences.zh: 齊兵退據相國城及金城。

translations.literal: Qi troops retreated to hold Xianguo city and Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi army fell back to Xianguo city and Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 明徹令軍中益修攻具，又遏肥水灌城，城中苦濕，多腹疾，手足皆腫，死者十六七。

translations.literal: Mingche ordered the army to further repair assault engines; he also dammed the Fei River to flood the city; in the city they suffered from damp; many had belly sickness; hands and feet all swelled; sixty or seventy percent died.
translations.idiomatic: Mingche strengthened the siege engines and dammed the Fei to flood the city. Damp and disease swept the garrison—bellies swelled, limbs ballooned—and six or seven in ten died.

sentences.zh: 會齊遣大將皮景和率兵數十萬來援，去壽春三十里，頓軍不進。

translations.literal: It happened that Qi sent the great general Pi Jinghe leading several hundred thousand troops as relief; thirty li from Shouchun they halted the army and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Qi sent Grand General Pi Jinghe with an army in the hundreds of thousands. He halted thirty li from Shouchun and would not advance.

sentences.zh: 諸將咸曰：「計將安出？」

translations.literal: The generals all said: "What plan shall we adopt?"
translations.idiomatic: The generals asked, "What is the plan?"

sentences.zh: 明徹曰：「兵貴在速，而彼結營不進，自挫其鋒，吾知其不敢戰明矣。」

translations.literal: Mingche said: "In warfare speed is prized, yet they have encamped and do not advance—they have blunted their own edge; I know clearly they dare not give battle."
translations.idiomatic: Mingche said, "Speed is everything in war. They have camped and stalled—they have blunted themselves. I know they will not fight."

sentences.zh: 於是躬擐甲胄，四面疾攻，城中震恐，一鼓而禽王琳等送建鄴。

translations.literal: Thereupon he personally donned armor, attacked swiftly on four sides; within the city there was shaking fear; at one drum-strike he captured Wang Lin and others and sent them to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: He donned armor himself and attacked on four sides. The city shook with fear. At one drumbeat he took Wang Lin alive and sent him to Jianye.

sentences.zh: 景和懼而遁走。

translations.literal: Jinghe in fear fled and absconded.
translations.idiomatic: Jinghe fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 詔以為車騎大將軍、豫州刺史，增封並前三千五百戶。

translations.literal: An edict made him Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Yuzhou; added enfeoffment together with prior fief totaling three thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and inspector of Yuzhou, with fiefs totaling thirty-five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 遣謁者蕭淳就壽陽授策，明徹于城南設壇，士卒二十萬，陳旗鼓戈甲，登壇拜受，成禮而退。

translations.literal: He sent the protocol officer Xiao Chun to Shouyang to present the tally; Mingche set up an altar south of the city; two hundred thousand soldiers; arrayed drums, banners, spears and armor; he ascended the altar, bowed and received, completed the rites and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Xiao Chun to Shouyang with the imperial tally. Mingche raised an altar south of the city before two hundred thousand men in full arms, mounted the altar, bowed, received the commission, and withdrew when the rites were done.

sentences.zh: 六年，自壽陽入朝，輿駕幸其第，賜鍾磬一部。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he entered court from Shouyang; the imperial carriage visited his residence; he was granted one set of bells and chime-stones.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he returned from Shouyang to court. The emperor visited his home and gave him a set of ritual bells and stones.

sentences.zh: 七年，進攻彭城，軍至呂梁，又大破齊軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he advanced to attack Pengcheng; the army reached Lüliang and again greatly defeated the Qi army.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven he marched on Pengcheng, reached Lüliang, and routed the Qi army again.

sentences.zh: 八年，進位司空，給大都督鈇鉞、龍麾。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he advanced in rank to Minister of Works; granted the great commander's axe and battle-ax and dragon ensign.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight he was promoted to Minister of Works and given the great commander's axe and dragon banners.

sentences.zh: 尋授都督、南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed area commander and Inspector of South Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made area commander and inspector of South Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 及周滅齊，宣帝將事徐、兗。

translations.literal: When Zhou destroyed Qi, Emperor Xuan was about to undertake affairs in Xu and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou destroyed Qi, Emperor Xuan was about to undertake affairs in Xu and Yan.

sentences.zh: 九年，詔明徹北侵，令其世子慧覺攝行州事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, an edict ordered Mingche to invade northward and ordered his heir Huijue to act in charge of provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, an edict ordered Mingche to invade northward and ordered his heir Huijue to act in charge of provincial affairs.

sentences.zh: 軍至呂梁，周徐州總管梁士彥率眾拒戰，明徹頻破之。

translations.literal: When the army reached Lüliang, Liang Shiyan, the Zhou area commander of Xuzhou, led troops to resist in battle, and Mingche repeatedly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Lüliang, Liang Shiyan, the Zhou area commander of Xuzhou, led troops to resist in battle, and Mingche repeatedly defeated him.

sentences.zh: 仍迮清水以灌其城，攻之甚急，環列舟艦於城下。

translations.literal: He then dammed the Qingshui to flood the city, attacked it very urgently, and arrayed ships all around below the city.
translations.idiomatic: He then dammed the Qingshui to flood the city, attacked it very urgently, and arrayed ships all around below the city.

sentences.zh: 周遣上大將軍王軌救之。

translations.literal: Zhou sent Supreme Grand General Wang Gui to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou sent Supreme Grand General Wang Gui to rescue it.

sentences.zh: 軌輕行自清水入淮口，橫流豎木，以鐵鎖貫車輪，遏斷船路。

translations.literal: Gui traveled light from the Qingshui to the Huai mouth, planted timbers across the current, threaded iron chains through cartwheels, and blocked the ship route.
translations.idiomatic: Gui traveled light from the Qingshui to the Huai mouth, planted timbers across the current, threaded iron chains through cartwheels, and blocked the ship route.

sentences.zh: 諸將聞之甚恐，議欲破堰拔軍，以舫載馬。

translations.literal: When the generals heard this, they were very frightened and discussed breaking the dam and withdrawing the army, using barges to carry the horses.
translations.idiomatic: When the generals heard this, they were very frightened and discussed breaking the dam and withdrawing the army, using barges to carry the horses.

sentences.zh: 馬明戍裴子烈曰：「君若決堰下船，船必傾倒，豈可得乎？

translations.literal: Pei Zilie of Maming Garrison said, “If you breach the dam and send the ships down, the ships will certainly overturn; how could this be possible?
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zilie of Maming Garrison said, “If you breach the dam and send the ships down, the ships will certainly overturn; how could this be possible?

sentences.zh: 不如前遣馬出。」

translations.literal: It would be better to send the horses out ahead.”
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to send the horses out ahead.”

sentences.zh: 適會明徹苦背疾甚篤，知事不濟，遂從之。

translations.literal: Just then Mingche was suffering severely from a back ailment and knew the affair could not succeed, so he followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Mingche was suffering severely from a back ailment and knew the affair could not succeed, so he followed this advice.

sentences.zh: 乃遣蕭摩訶帥馬軍數千前還，明徹仍自決其堰，乘水力以退軍。

translations.literal: He then sent Xiao Mohe to lead several thousand cavalry back first, while Mingche himself breached the dam and used the force of the water to withdraw the army.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Xiao Mohe to lead several thousand cavalry back first, while Mingche himself breached the dam and used the force of the water to withdraw the army.

sentences.zh: 及至清口，水力微，舟艦並不得度，眾軍皆潰。

translations.literal: When they reached Qingkou, the force of the water was slight, the boats and ships could not all pass through, and all the armies collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Qingkou, the force of the water was slight, the boats and ships could not all pass through, and all the armies collapsed.

sentences.zh: 明徹窮蹙，乃就執。

translations.literal: Mingche was trapped and hard pressed, and so he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Mingche was trapped and hard pressed, and so he was captured.

sentences.zh: 周封懷德郡公，位大將軍。

translations.literal: Zhou enfeoffed him as Duke of Huaide Commandery and gave him the rank of Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou enfeoffed him as Duke of Huaide Commandery and gave him the rank of Grand General.

sentences.zh: 以憂遘疾，卒於長安，後故吏盜其柩歸。

translations.literal: From grief he fell ill and died at Chang’an; afterward, his former officials stole his coffin and brought it back.
translations.idiomatic: From grief he fell ill and died at Chang’an; afterward, his former officials stole his coffin and brought it back.

sentences.zh: 至德元年，詔追封邵陵侯，以其息慧覺嗣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhide, an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Marquis of Shaoling and made his son Huijue succeed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhide, an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Marquis of Shaoling and made his son Huijue succeed him.

sentences.zh: 裴子烈字大士，河東聞喜人。

translations.literal: Pei Zilie, styled Dashi, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zilie, styled Dashi, came from Wenxi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 梁員外散騎常侍猗之子。

translations.literal: Son of Yi, supernumerary palace attendant for casual riding under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He was the son of Yi, Liang's supernumerary palace attendant for casual riding.

sentences.zh: 少孤，有志氣，以驍勇聞。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he had aspiration and spirit; he was known for fierce courage.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he had force of character and was known for valor.

sentences.zh: 位北譙太守，岳陽內史，封海安伯。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Administrator of North Qiao, Interior Minister of Yueyang, and was enfeoffed as Earl of Hai'an.
translations.idiomatic: He served as administrator of North Qiao and interior minister of Yueyang and was enfeoffed as Earl of Hai'an.

sentences.zh: 論曰：古人云：「知臣莫若君」，書曰：「知人則哲」，觀夫陳武論將，而周、侯遇禍，有以知斯言之非妄矣。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: The ancients said, "No one knows his ministers like their lord," and the Documents says, "Knowing men is wisdom." Looking at Emperor Wu of Chen's judgments of his generals and at the disasters that befell Zhou and Hou, one can know that these sayings are not false.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal states: The ancients said, "No one knows his ministers like their lord," and the Documents says, "Knowing men is wisdom." Looking at Emperor Wu of Chen's judgments of his generals and at the disasters that befell Zhou and Hou, one can know that these sayings are not false.

sentences.zh: 若不然者，亦何以驅駕雄傑，而創基撥亂者乎。

translations.literal: If it were not so, how could one drive and harness heroic champions and found a base amid turmoil?
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise how could he have rallied heroes and carved an empire from chaos?

sentences.zh: 故瑱、頠並自奔囚，翻同有亂，奭、量望風景附，自等誠臣，良有以也。

translations.literal: Therefore Zhen and Wei each on their own fled as prisoners, yet likewise possessed disorder; Fa and Liang saw the wind and submitted to attach themselves—they equaled themselves to true ministers; there was good reason.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Zhen and Wei fled into captivity yet still carried rebellion in them, while Fa and Liang submitted at the first sign of fortune and called themselves loyal servants—each for understandable reasons.

sentences.zh: 昭達勤王之略，遠符耿弇，行己之方，頗同吳漢，既眇而貴，亦黥而王，吉凶之算，豈人事也。

translations.literal: Zhaoda's strategy in supporting the sovereign far matched Geng Yan; his manner in conduct rather resembled Wu Han; blind in one eye yet ennobled, tattooed yet made king—the reckoning of fortune and disaster—how is it a matter of human affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoda's loyal strategy recalled Geng Yan of Han; his conduct resembled Wu Han. Blinded yet ennobled, branded yet made a king—whether fortune or ruin is settled cannot be merely a matter of human effort.

sentences.zh: 明徹屬運否之期，當辟土之任，才非韓、白，識暗孫、吳，知進而不知止，知得而不知喪，犯斯不韙，師亡國蹙，宜矣哉。

translations.literal: Mingche belonged to an age when fortune turned adverse; he bore the charge to open territory; his talent was not that of Han Xin or Bai Qi; his knowledge fell short of Sun Wu; he knew advance but not stopping, knew gain but not loss; violating this great fault, the army perished and the state was pressed—fitting indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Mingche lived in a season of ill fortune yet held the charge to expand the realm. He was no Han Xin or Bai Qi, nor a strategist on par with Sun Wu. He knew how to advance but not when to halt, how to win but not how to lose. To break that rule was to lose the army and corner the state—and so it proved.
